articles.title: Ombudsman to step up lifestyle checks on BIR, BOC execs amid bribery reports
articles.summary: The Office of the Ombudsman will conduct intensified lifestyle check on officials of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and the Bureau of Customs (BOC) amid reports of its officials collecting…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 3:27pm

The Office of the Ombudsman will conduct intensified lifestyle check on officials of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and the Bureau of Customs (BOC) amid reports of its officials collecting bribe money, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said Friday.
Remulla made the announcement during his town hall meeting with the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industries (PCCI).

It also comes just a day after the Marcos administration announced that erstwhile BIR Commissioner Charlito Mendoza will move to the Bureau of Customs, while Finance Department official Rolando Ligon Jr. will take over as the country's top taxman. Both Mendoza and Ligon were sworn into office on Friday.

"We will intensify our lifestyle checks on officials of the BIR and the BOC, the two agencies that [are] entrusted with collecting the money that builds our roads, our schools, and our hospitals. That money belongs to the Filipino people," Remulla said.
Remulla said he has received reports of government officials collecting illegal fees with no receipts, and instances wherein these fees even exceed the amounts duly collected with receipts.
"Walang lehitimong bayad sa gobyerno na walang resibo. Bawat piso na binabayad sa estado, dapat may resibo,” Remulla said.
(No government transaction is paid without a receipt. Every peso paid to the government must have a receipt.)
"Ang bayad na walang resibo ay hindi buwis. It's corruption," Remulla added.
(Those fees without receipts are not taxes.)
Remulla said these issues are what the Investment Ombudsman, a new unit under the Ombudsman, seeks to address.
The Ombudsman said businesses should be able to feel safe to report government officials who try to collect bribes from them.
"The Ombudsman's job is to protect the people, protect the businesses that employ them, feed them and build communities," Remulla said. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Meralco rates up in November as peso drop, Middle East crisis persist
articles.summary: Driving this month’s overall rate increase was the generation charge which went up due to higher costs of power suppliers still affected by the peso depreciation and the crisis in the Middle East

blocks.text: (This is a press release from the Manila Electric Company.)

MANILA, Philippines – The Manila Electric Company (Meralco) announced on Friday, November 13 an upward adjustment of P0.4895 per kilowatt hour (kWh) in the electricity rate for the month of November, bringing the overall rate for a typical household to P15.5510 from P15.0615 per kWh in October.
For residential customers who are consuming 200 kWh, this adjustment translates to an increase of around P98 in the total electricity bill.

Driving this month’s overall rate increase was the generation charge which went up by P0.4344 per kWh mainly due to higher costs of power suppliers, which remain affected by the peso depreciation and the ongoing crisis in the Middle East.

Charges from First Gas/Prime CoreGen went up by P2.9241 per kWh mainly due to higher fuel costs resulting from Malampaya natural gas quarterly repricing and increase in the price of liquefied natural gas (LNG). First Gas/Prime CoreGen’s LNG use went up from 24% to 44%, as it needed to supplement Malampaya supply with imported gas. The peso also depreciated to its lowest level during the period, affecting around 86% of First Gas/Prime CoreGen’s costs that were dollar denominated.

Charges from the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM) also increased by P4.3946 per kWh, as average demand in Luzon rose by around 769 MW brought about by warmer temperatures in October 2026, which were even warmer than in October 2024, the last El Niño event.
Meanwhile, charges from Power Supply Agreements (PSAs) decreased by P0.2769 per kWh owing to higher average PSA dispatch.
For this period, First Gas/Prime CoreGen, PSAs, and WESM accounted for around 24%, 73%, and 3%, respectively, of Meralco’s total supply requirements.

blocks.caption: [READOUT] The race to deliver cheaper power

blocks.text: Contributing to the overall rate increase were higher taxes and other pass-through charges which had a net increase of P0.2165 per kWh. This is mainly due to higher taxes resulting from the lower utilization of indigenous natural gas, which is exempt from value-added tax (VAT).

These also include the slight increase in charges from the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) of P0.0080 per kWh. The transmission charge went up by P0.1721 per kWh following the Energy Regulatory Commission’s (ERC) approval of higher Maximum Allowable Revenue (MAR) for NGCP. This, however, was largely offset by the P0.1641 per kWh reduction in the ancillary service charge because of the suspension of the Reserve Market starting October 14.

Pass-through charges for generation, and transmission and ancillary service are paid by Meralco to the power suppliers and the NGCP, respectively, while taxes, universal charges, and other public policy charges are all remitted to the government and the relevant agencies.

This month’s rates also reflect the implementation of new distribution tariffs approved by the ERC for the First Regulatory Period (1RP), which resulted to a minimal increase in distribution, supply and metering (DSM) charges of residential customers. For those with consumption of 200 kWh, the adjustment is equivalent to a slight increase of P0.0096 per kWh.
Following Meralco’s implementation of its 1RP rates, regulatory reset fees adjustments shall also be set to zero starting this month, from the previous rate of P0.0023 per kWh.
Beginning this November, Meralco will also implement another refund related to its Actual Weighted Average Tariff (AWAT), tempering the upward movement in other components.

As approved by the ERC, the latest AWAT refund — which translates to a P0.1733 per kWh downward adjustment for residential customers — will be implemented over six (6) months or until the full amount has been fully refunded.

This AWAT refund covers Meralco’s application for the Lapsed Period from January to June 2026 and was filed in compliance with previous ERC orders for the years when distribution utilities like Meralco did not have a rate reset. Subsequently, adjustments had to be filed to the ERC to cover the difference between Meralco’s AWAT and the Meralco’s approved distribution tariff of P1.3522 per kWh during the Lapsed Period.

Meralco likewise is continuously implementing two simultaneous AWAT refunds–equivalent to a total of P1.0139 per kWh for residential customers. These two AWAT refunds cover the Lapsed Periods from July2022 to December 2025.
In accordance with ERC’s directive, Meralco reminds its customers of the extended payment due dates for unpaid electricity bills to avoid possible service disconnection.
Unpaid electricity bills from May to July 2026 must be settled on or before November 26, 2026, while those covering August to October 2026 must be paid on or before December 26, 2026.

For customers with monthly electricity consumption of 200 kWh or below, the suspension of disconnection activities has been extended until December, provided that all unpaid bills from May to July 2026 are settled on or before November 26, 2026.
Meanwhile, customers with monthly consumption exceeding 200 kWh are advised to settle any outstanding balances within the prescribed period to avoid service disconnection.

For customers who may need assistance or need flexible payment arrangements, they can reach Meralco through its different customer touch points. Payments may be made conveniently through the My Meralco app or any authorized payment partner. Customers who may need assistance or flexible paymentarrangements may reach out through Facebook Messenger, email customercare@meralco.com.ph, or visit the nearest Meralco Business Center.
During the ASEAN Summit on November 16 to 18, all Meralco Business Centers will remain open from 7 am to 5 pm, with a skeletal workforce. All customer transactions will continue to be accommodated.

For electricity service concerns, customers can report through the My Meralco app or through Meralco’s official social media accounts on Facebook (www.facebook.com/meralco) and X (@meralco). They may also text their concerns to 0920-9716211 or 0917-5516211 or contact the Meralco Hotline at 16211. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Microsoft outage spills into Asia-Pacific business hours despite ‘partial recovery’
articles.summary: In its latest update, Microsoft says it had applied adjustments to the affected servers, but they did not result in sustained recovery

blocks.text: MICROSOFT IN BEIJING. A person walks past a Microsoft sign at its office building in Beijing, China on May 25, 2023.
Tingshu Wang/Reuters
In its latest update, Microsoft says it had applied adjustments to the affected servers, but they did not result in sustained recovery

items: Microsoft services, including Outlook and Teams, experienced a significant outage affecting users in the US and Asia-Pacific, attributed to server problems.
The outage impacted various sectors, including government agencies and businesses like OpenAI and Anthropic, raising concerns about Microsoft's reliability due to multiple disruptions this year.
Microsoft is working on improving infrastructure stability and has stated that the outage is not due to malicious activity, while some partial recovery has been observed.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

A disruption of Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot stretched into Asia-Pacific business hours on Friday, November 13, after affecting thousands of US users, as the tech giant struggled to fix server problems it blamed for the outage.

The outage hit government agencies in Australia, Japan and the United States, as well as companies including OpenAI and Anthropic. It is the second disruption to Microsoft’s 365 services this year, raising concerns that repeated failures could push corporate clients to question Microsoft’s reliability.

In its latest update, Microsoft said it had applied adjustments to the affected servers, but they did not result in sustained recovery. It said it had observed some partial recovery in the regions where it applied the adjustments.
“We’re reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability,” the company said on X.

Downdetector, which tracks outages by collating status reports from a number of sources, showed more than 18,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US at 11:30 pm ET (0430 GMT; 12:30 pm Philippine time). It also showed outages for several Microsoft services in the Asia-Pacific region, including India, Australia and Japan, early Friday local time.
At its peak, Downdetector showed more than 130,000 reports of Outlook problems in the US around 1 pm ET on Thursday. The outage has lasted for about 12 hours.

In a service health notice, Microsoft said features of Microsoft 365 services that depended on Exchange Online and email were affected, while elements that did not rely on Exchange Online remained functional. Exchange Online is the company’s cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks.
The company added that it was “not aware” of any malicious activity that was causing the outage.
Australian Home Affairs and Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said that Microsoft believed it was not dealing with a cyberattack.
“They believe they are dealing in some ways similar to what we saw with respect to CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry,” Burke said at a press conference.
“The impact that they are dealing with … is very much on email systems,” the minister added.
Australia’s spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught up in the outage on Friday.

The CrowdStrike malfunction of 2024 was one of the largest internet disruptions, hobbling technology systems in hospitals, banks, and airports, highlighting the vulnerability of the world’s interconnected technologies.
The US House of Representatives said the outage impacted its users and its engineers were working with Microsoft.
Japanese Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki told reporters that the outage was affecting the government’s information system infrastructure.
US AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic said they had faced issues with Microsoft connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase agreement transaction it had already scheduled, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters, declining to provide the name of the company.
Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro, said investors would likely look past the outage but that repeated disruptions could hurt Microsoft over time.
“I think investors will take this in their stride for now, because very few of these customers can realistically walk away from the Microsoft ecosystem overnight,” Gilbert said.

“The bigger worry is that this isn’t the first 365 outage this year, and if reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider’s hands. The market will want to see Microsoft prove it can keep the lights on before it asks customers to spend more on Copilot.”
Microsoft faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and also in October last year.
Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software, and a range of industries worldwide.

Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on November 12, rescheduled it to November 16 citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage. – Rappler.com

articles.title: A baffling trail from Australia to Singapore: what is Megaspeed, the company implicated in downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?
articles.summary:
Few solid clues have emerged as to the true nature of Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese spy

  • Get our
articles.byline: Kate Lamb, Josh Butler and agencies

blocks.text: A lottery retailer in rural Australia, a dilapidated storefront in Kuala Lumpur, and a near-empty office in Singapore: the global facades of Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, form a puzzling corporate picture.

The company, which is registered in Singapore, has registered affiliates across the US, Asia and Australia, but individuals at its offices say they know nothing about the cloud computing firm at the centre of a global spy scandal.

On Friday Huang resigned as chief executive of the chip manufacturer Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two company employees. US intelligence agencies believe Huang had been targeted by Alice Huang (no relation), the former director of Megaspeed International.
US officials believe Huang was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times has reported.
On Thursday, Singaporean authorities said Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the city state after a 2025 investigation into the company.

Singapore police said last October they were investigating Megaspeed over “suspected breaches of our domestic laws” after a US senator requested the commerce department investigate whether the firm had diverted Nvidia chips.

The ministry of home affairs said this week it had held Alice Huang’s passport from June 2025 until February over “potential false declarations” related to Megaspeed. Eventually, she was released with a stern warning.

blocks.caption: Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

blocks.text: Earlier this week, authorities in Taiwan said she had also been barred from re-entering there.
On Friday Malaysia said it was investigating a subsidiary of Megaspeed International over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.
Baffling trails
Across the region, Megaspeed’s activities remain obscure.

In Sydney, no signage, mailbox or physical presence suggests the company at the epicentre of one of the biggest stories in the world is located on the 10th floor of an office building in the city centre.

“Do you have an appointment?” a receptionist asked when the Guardian visted the office, home to numerous businesses. It hummed with activity but no one had heard of Megaspeed Australia or its listed director, 29-year-old Kai Kang.

Megaspeed International filed papers in the US state of Delaware ⁠and with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (Asic), showing the affiliates were created in 2024. Both filings list the Shanghai-born Kang as the sole company officer, either as ​director or president.
The Australian ‌filing also lists the Singapore-based parent as ‌the company’s stockholder.
Reuters ‌visited the home address provided on the filings for the affiliates – a small store, a news agency and lottery retailer, in Seymour, Victoria, about an hour’s drive north of Melbourne.
A woman, who identified herself as Kang’s mother, said she had run the business for about 16 years. She said Kang was based in Shanghai and did not know anything about the Singaporean company.
“He doesn’t have any business here,” she said, adding that Kang had completed his master’s degree at Shanghai University.

blocks.caption: Jensen Huang at a restaurant in Taipei last year with Alice Huang, no relation, who is accused of being a Chinese spy. Photograph: CTI/AFPTV/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: He had visited his parents most recently in August and September, she said.
She said she knew about Nvidia and Megaspeed but her son had nothing to do with the company in Singapore.

It is not the only perplexing finding that journalists have encountered when trying to track down representatives of Megaspeed, which in the past three years has been one of Nvidia’s biggest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5bn in AI chips and advanced hardware.

The Straits Times reported that Swiftdata, the little-known company that owns Megaspeed, had a registered business address in Singapore, but an interior design firm said it had occupied the premises for more than four years.
Last year the New York Times visited Megaspeed’s Singapore headquarters, located in the central business district, but found only two employees present.

And in neighbouring Malaysia, the Times found that one of Megaspeed’s offices was a dilapidated storefront in the capital. Another was located in a shopping mall. When one employee emerged in the mall, she was asked what the company did.
“It’s not clear,” she said.
Kang is also registered as a director in Megaspeed’s Malaysian, Indonesian and Thai units.
Kang has not been accused of any wrongdoing. Attempts to contact him were unsuccessful.
Australian concerns

In Australia, a former intelligence officer said they expected Australian security agencies would have sought briefings from overseas counterparts about Megaspeed or undertaken their own assessments of the local subsidiary this week.

Michael Shoebridge, the director of the security thinktank Strategic Analysis Australia and a former deputy of the Australian Signals Directorate and the Defence Intelligence Organisation (Asio), said key details about Megaspeed’s relationship with Chinese intelligence remained unclear.
He suggested it would be “credible” to assess the company as a “front for Chinese intelligence” but nothing was certain.

The Chinese government has flatly rejected any claims Alice Huang was a spy. A foreign ministry spokesperson, Guo Jiakun, said earlier this week the allegations were “unsubstantiated” and “nothing but smears against China”.
Shoebridge said Megaspeed’s Australian operation could be a legitimate business or designed to make the Singapore-based parent company “look credible” by having overseas affiliates.
Asio declined to comment when asked if it was examining Megaspeed Australia. The office of the Australian home affairs minister, Tony Burke, also declined to comment.

The acting prime minister, Richard Marles, was asked on ABC TV this week whether there had been discussions inside government “about some of the potential spying that could be taking place within Australian companies”.

On ABC radio, Marles, speaking generally, said: “We are living in a world where there is more espionage than there has been for a long time. A lot of that is particularly around emerging technologies.”
The federal opposition said any potential foreign interference “must be taken seriously”.

Megaspeed International did not respond to a request for comment or information about its Australian arm. Messages to a Facebook page that last posted in 2020 and an associated email address went unanswered.

Asic documents show Kang was born in 1996 in Shanghai and has been listed as Megaspeed Australia’s director since the company was registered. They reveal Megaspeed International owns all 10,000 shares of Megaspeed Australia’s stocks, for which it paid $1m.

blocks.text: November 13, 2026
Activist Sonam Wangchuk decries 'house arrest' ahead of controversial regional elections

Indian activist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk has claimed that he has been put under a house arrest with "dozens of armed guards" stationed outside his home in Ladakh, the country's remote Himalayan territory.
"I am under house arrest," the 60-year-old wrote on X late Thursday night, alongside a video message.

"There are 20 to 25 police and paramilitary personnel outside the house," Wangchuk said, adding that armed personnel were standing guard outside his house, "in all directions." He shared visuals purporting to show the restrictions.
Wangchuk also said his X and YouTube reach had been "drastically suppressed" as he called on supporters to share his message.
Ladakh's hill council election row
Wangchuk's allegation followed a day after police removed him from a protest site ahead of a planned sit-in demonstration about the timing of hill council elections, slated for December 4.

The climate crusader, along with Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), Ladakh's main civil society groups, have raised concerns about holding the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council elections, covering eight districts, at a time of the year when the high-altitude desert region sees a harsh winter and a large seasonal migration.
Ladakh activists say the sub-zero temperatures and winter migration could result in a low voter turnout.

"December and January are the coldest and snowiest months with temperature dipping below -30 degrees Celsius in many places and close to half the population migrates out of Ladakh for education, vacation, pilgrimage etc," Wangchuk said on X in a public appeal with LAB and KDA, calling for the elections to be deferred.

Ladakh police have said that Wangchuk was "advised to stay his residence" in accordance with prohibitory orders issued by Ladakh's Chief Electoral Officer and the Leh District Magistrate ahead of the elections.
Ladakh was split from Indian-administered Kashmir after New Delhi stripped the disputed region's statehood and semi-autonomy in 2019.
Ladakh was categorized as a "Union Territory" with Leh and Kargil being its two main districts.

The LAB and KDA have been demanding statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Indian constitution, which allows indigenous tribal people to make their own laws and policies on land.
Wangchuk said people of Ladakh were protesting the manner in which the hill council elections were being conducted and also the type of councils.
In his Thursday night message, Wangchuk described the council elections as "phoney" and the councils as "disempowered."
On Wednesday, Wangchuk had also raised questions over the delay in a report of a judicial inquiry commission looking into the deadly 2025 Leh protests over statehood demands.
Wangchuk linked the Thursday restrictions against him to the "uncomfortable questions" he had asked.

Meanwhile, Ladakh authorities have urged people to "participate enthusiastically" in the upcoming elections and have deemed the councils as "an important milestone in strengthening democratic institutions" in the region.

articles.title: Who is Gamaliel Cordoba, the new SC associate justice?
articles.summary: Gamaliel Asis Cordoba has been named the new Supreme Court (SC) associate justice on Friday, November 13, 2026. He will succeed SC Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who will retire on November 16,…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 2:55pm
Gamaliel Asis Cordoba has been named the new Supreme Court (SC) associate justice on Friday, November 13, 2026.
He will succeed SC Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who will retire on November 16, 2026.
Cordoba currently serves as the chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA), having been appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on October 21, 2022.

Prior to his appointment at COA, Cordoba served the longest term as commissioner of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC), serving across the administrations of Marcos and former Presidents Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, Benigno Aquino III, and Rodrigo Duterte.

“His 13-year stint with the NTC witnessed landmark projects resulting in the country’s marked improvement in Internet speeds through the streamlining of permits for the construction of telecommunication towers and fiber optic installations,” Cordoba’s profile read on the COA website.

“The country’s fixed broadband and mobile internet speeds remarkably improved globally under his leadership with Ookla Speedtest Global Index now ranking the Philippines 41st out of 180 countries globally for fixed broadband and 79th out of 140 countries for mobile,” it added.
From 2008 to 2009, Cordoba also served on the Board of Directors of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR).

He also held several key positions under the Arroyo administration at the Office of the President, serving as Appointments Secretary from 2006 to 2007, Undersecretary from 2003 to 2006, and Assistant Executive Secretary from 2002 to 2003.
Prior to those posts, he served as a Director at the Office of the Presidential Chief of Staff from 2001 to 2002.

“Chairperson Cordoba served in Ex Oficio capacity representing the Office of the President as Director of the Philippine National Railways; Director of the Maritime Industry Authority; Member of the Presidential Committee on Good Governance and Execom Member of the Technology and Livelihood Resource Center,” his profile read.
In 2010, Cordoba was awarded the Presidential Medal of Merit by Arroyo and received the Radio Award from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications of Japan.

Cordoba earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in Economics from the Ateneo de Manila University, where he also completed his Juris Doctor in 1996 before passing the Philippine Bar Examination in 1997. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Vice Adm. Alan Javier, the former chief of the military’s Western Command (Wescom), formally assumed command of the Philippine Navy on Friday, succeeding Vice Adm. Jose Ma.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Vice Adm. Alan Javier, the former chief of the military’s Western Command (Wescom), formally assumed command of the Philippine Navy on Friday, succeeding Vice Adm. Jose Ma. Ambrosio Ezpeleta, who retired after more than 35 years of military service.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. presided over the change of command and retirement ceremony at the Philippine Navy headquarters in Manila on Nov. 13.

Before his appointment, Javier headed Wescom, which oversees military operations in Palawan and the West Philippine Sea, where Chinese vessels have repeatedly challenged Philippine maritime activities.
He also previously served as commander of the Western Naval Command, formerly known as Naval Forces West, and as chief of Naval Staff.
The Department of National Defense (DND) welcomed Javier’s appointment, citing his experience in naval operations and military leadership.

“Vice Admiral Javier brings with him the operational urgency and strategic direction needed to lead the Philippine Navy and sustain our naval operations,” Defense spokesperson Arsenio Andolong said in a statement.
Javier takes over the Navy as the Philippines continues to modernize its maritime forces and strengthen its presence in the West Philippine Sea amid persistent tensions with China.
Beijing claims nearly the entire South China Sea, including waters within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone, despite a 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated its sweeping maritime claims.
The DND also thanked Ezpeleta for his more than 35 years of military service as he retired from the Armed Forces of the Philippines. /mr

Release / SC PIO
MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Commission on Audit chair Gamaliel Cordoba as Supreme Court associate justice.
Cordoba will replace Amy Lazaro-Javier, who is set to retire on November 16 upon reaching the mandatory retirement age of 70.
His appointment was announced on Friday, November 13, during a briefing at the International Media Center with Palace Press Secretary Claire Castro.

Prior to his role at COA, Cordoba was the Commissioner of the National Telecommunications Commission from 2009 until 2022. On May 5, 2020, the NTC under Cordoba issued a cease-and-desist order forcing ABS-CBN off the airwaves immediately after its franchise expired on May 4, 2020.
This will be the third appointment of Marcos to the Supreme Court. He now has two appointed Associate Justices and one Chief Justice.
Marcos is also expected to appoint another Associate Justice left vacant by now-Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda. — with reports from Ian Laqui.

articles.summary: Former CEO Jensen Huang and US commerce secretary to appear before Congress amid bipartisan concern that America’s security was put at risk

blocks.text: Nvidia’s ousted CEO Jensen Huang and Donald Trump’s commerce secretary are expected to testify before Congress in the coming weeks, as the fallout from Huang’s reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy reverberated across the US, sparking bipartisan concerns for national security and calls for a tougher stance against Beijing.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Huang and Nvidia must answer as to whether America’s security had been jeopardised, adding that the Trump administration also must account for what it did once it learned about Huang’s reported relationship with Alice Huang, who is accused of spying for China.

Donald Trump’s close ties with Jensen Huang have also come under renewed scrutiny as a timeline of the saga started to emerge. The president called Jensen Huang two days before he stepped down and urged him to fight for his job, the New York Times has reported.

On Thursday, Schumer questioned what Donald Trump knew when he personally invited Jensen Huang aboard Air Force One on a state visit to Beijing earlier this year, adding: “Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships.”
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said he had demanded a classified briefing for all members of Congress about Nvidia.

The scandal has also drawn in Trump’s commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, after criticism of his department’s oversight of Nvidia’s exports to China and its refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist.
“Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the banking committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News.

Republican Tim Scott, the Senate banking committee chair said he had sent letters asking Lutnick and Jensen Huang to appear before him because: “Recent reports raise serious ‌concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology.”
Scott said he would consider subpoenaing Huang if he did not voluntarily appear. “The American people deserve answers,” Scott said.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday, and was replaced on an interim basis by chief financial officer Colette Kress after reports emerged of multiple affairs, key among them with Alice Huang, who is no relation but is suspected to be a Chinese spy.

The statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal conduct revelations, instead paying tribute to Huang’s “profound” contributions to the company he co-founded.
House foreign affairs chair Brian Mast, a Republican, said on Thursday that congressional staff had spoken to Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for Jensen Huang’s testimony.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday there was now growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China.

Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against ​China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to ‌limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does ‌not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

“The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here,” Johnson told reporters ‌at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China’s access to the advanced technology. “I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.“

Chinese AI companies are now trying to secure Nvidia chip capacity outside China, amid growing concern that the gap in US export controls may now be closed after the scandal, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
Beijing has also stepped up efforts to develop domestic alternatives, including through Huawei, although analysts say Chinese chips remain less efficient for training advanced AI models.
Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four bills on chip exports, according to statements issued since Monday.
On Chinese social media, many expressed surprise at what they see as the swift resignation, and mourned the sudden end of an era that lasted for over three decades.
News of his resignation attracted more than 400m posts overnight on Chinese microblogging platform Weibo.

Huang had enjoyed rock-star status in China, where his visits drew crowds seeking selfies and autographs and his casual outings became social-media sensations. During a January 2026 visit, opportunistic sellers advertised photographs with him for 25,000 yuan ($3,700), while a Beijing restaurant launched a special menu costing more than 400 yuan after he ate there.
Additional reporting by Yu-chen Li

articles.title: Small islands aim to use remittances to fund climate resilience
articles.summary: Their plan would create the first platform to use earnings sent by the overseas diaspora rather than international development aid to build a permanent endowment fund for climate resilience

blocks.text: FLOODED. Local boy Ratusela Waqanaceva, 14, wades through seawater flooding over an ineffective sea wall at high tide, as the community experiences flooding in Serua Village, Fiji, July 15, 2022.
Loren Elliott/Reuters
Their plan would create the first platform to use earnings sent by the overseas diaspora rather than international development aid to build a permanent endowment fund for climate resilience

items: A group of Small Island Developing States (SIDS) is proposing a fund to raise around $3 billion annually through a charge on remittances from islanders abroad to enhance climate resilience.

The initiative aims to create a permanent endowment fund that would utilize remittances, which totaled approximately $22 billion from 2010 to 2023, to finance adaptation projects instead of relying solely on international aid.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ANTALYA, Turkey – A group of small island states aims to create a fund backed by a charge on money that islanders receive from abroad to eventually raise around $3 billion a year for projects to make their nations less vulnerable to climate change.
That would exceed the roughly $2 billion in international public adaptation finance they received in 2021-2022, according to a 2025 study by non-profit research group the Climate Policy Initiative.

Country representatives meeting until the end of next week in the Mediterranean city of Antalya in Turkey for COP31 climate talks are trying to agree ways to increase funding for adaptation to a warming world.
Representatives of Small Island Developing States, or SIDS, have decided they cannot wait for the long-running international debate on financing to deliver more help.

“We decided that there had to be a way that we can guarantee more reliable sources of funding for the islands,” Antigua and Barbuda’s UN ambassador Walton Webson said. “We cannot rely solely on development assistance again.”
“What we are now trying to do is create our own.”

The SIDS grouping brings together island nations in the Pacific, the Caribbean and the Atlantic, Indian Ocean, and South China Sea that are particularly vulnerable to the impact of rising sea levels as the planet warms.
Many of them also have large amounts of national debt that constrain their ability to invest in protection, such as measures to halt coastal erosion.
Webson said preliminary discussions had taken place with several development banks and a broader meeting with them and SIDS leaders was planned for January to try to make progress by COP32 in 2027.
Their plan would create the first platform to use earnings sent by the overseas diaspora rather than international development aid to build a permanent endowment fund for climate resilience.
Total remittances from the many islanders who have emigrated were around $22 billion and grew at a compound annual rate of 7% between 2010 and 2023, according to numbers provided by the SIDS group.
It aims for the planned platform to capture about a third of that total by its 10th year of operation.

Drafted with the help of non-profit organisation, the International Institute for Environment and Development, a first phase would draw on remittances to the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Jamaica and Guyana in year one. Fiji, Samoa and Tonga would be included in year two and Comoros, Cabo Verde and Mauritius in year three.
The SIDS platform would charge senders 3% per transaction, lower than average costs of around 5% to 9% across the markets studied.

The commercial sector in total charges up to $1.3 billion a year to cover transfer fees and foreign exchange margins, the SIDS document seen by Reuters showed. By contrast, multilateral climate funds approved just $202 million for SIDS in 2023.

After costs, 2 to 2.5 percentage points of each transaction would enter the fund, be held as an endowment and invested, seeking base-case returns of 6.5%. Of the returns, 85% would be spent on resilience measures and the rest held as a disaster reserve.

By year 10, the base-case scenario estimates the endowment would have reached $2.59 billion. Matching grants and other income streams such as tourism levies could take the total to $5.53 billion and generate $306 million a year in distributable surplus.
Leverage through tools such as guarantees could help mobilize up to $3.13 billion a year.
Palau’s President Surangel Whipps Jr said the small islands that did not create the climate crisis are expected to borrow more money to cope with it than those that did.

“This proposal turns that logic around. It takes money that is already ours, already flowing home across the Pacific, the Caribbean and beyond, and puts it to work for our own resilience,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Victoria election 2026: Labor and Greens trade accusations of ‘dodgy deals’ as preferences squabble puts key seats on the line
articles.summary:
Greens retaliate against Labor’s move to run an open ticket in Prahran by leaving the party off how-to-vote cards in 15 seats

The Greens have retaliated against Labor’s decision to run an…

blocks.text: The Greens have retaliated against Labor’s decision to run an open ticket in a key inner-city seat by refusing to direct preferences to the party in 15 electorates across the state at this month’s Victorian election.
The move has sparked a war of words between the two parties, with each accusing the other of striking a “dodgy deal” that could help the Liberals and One Nation get elected on 28 November.
On Friday, the Greens confirmed they would only be directing voters to number the Greens one and One Nation last across 15 electorates.

The decision follows Labor’s decision on Tuesday to run an open ticket in the inner Melbourne seat of Prahran, where the Greens had been counting on Labor preferences to win it back. It has been held by the Liberals on a tiny 1.3 per cent margin – after the Greens lost it at a byelection in 2025.
At the time, Greens leader Ellen Sandell told Guardian Australia Labor’s “unforgivable” decision could hand the upcoming election to a Liberal-One Nation coalition.
A Labor spokesperson turned the accusation back on the Greens on Friday, mirroring Sandell’s language.
“In one of the most consequential elections in Victoria’s history – the Greens have done a dodgy deal to help elect a Liberal One-Nation Government,” the spokesperson said.

“This is unforgivable and Victorians won’t forget it’s Ellen Sandell and the Greens to blame when Jess Wilson cuts our hospitals and schools – and One Nation winds back our nation leading reforms on women’s rights and Treaty.”
The Greens responded by accusing Labor of “lying to Victorian voters”.
“The Greens will be putting One Nation last in every single electorate across Victoria. We always encourage people to vote in line with their values,” their spokesperson said.
“After months of scaremongering about a Liberal-One Nation government, it is Labor who have done a dodgy backroom deal with the Liberals that could help elect one.”

The 15 electorates where the Greens will issue these how-to-vote cards are: Albert Park, Ashwood, Bellarine, Bendigo East, Bendigo West, Essendon, Euroa, Gippsland East, Mildura, Mornington, Point Cook, Polwarth, South Barwon, Tarneit, Werribee.

Labor fears the decision will particularly hurt their chances in Albert Park, Ashwood, Bellarine, the two Bendigo seats vacated by former premier Jacinta Allan and speaker Maree Edwards, and South Barwon.
The Coalition, meanwhile, is quietly confident it will improving its chances of fending off One Nation and snatching seats from Labor.

However, Tony Barry the Liberal strategist turned pollster with Redbridge and co-host of Guardian Australia’s Back to Back Barries podcast, said most Greens voters don’t closely follow their party’s how-to-vote cards.

“Historical preference flows from past state and federal elections shows about 85% of exhausted Greens votes flows to Labor and about 15% leakage to the Coalition and that rarely changes regardless of the particular circumstances,” Barry said.

But he said in Essendon, where Labor candidate Kat Theodosis is contesting the seat following Danny Pearson’s retirement, in a complex race involving the Liberals, One Nation and three independents candidates, it “might be enough to flip the seat to the Liberals.”

Meanwhile, the conservative Family First party is directing its preferences to Labor candidates affiliated with the Shop, Distributive and Allied Employees’ Association (SDA), placing them second on their how-to-vote cards. The cards feature an image of a baby next to the Labor candidate name with claims they have a “pro-life voting record”.

It prompted Pasoce Vale MP Anthony Cianflone, who is in a tight race against the Greens’ Angelica Panopoulos, to post a statement on social media saying he supported “women’s right to make their own decisions about their bodies and healthcare”.
“That’s why I have supported the Victorian Labor government’s reforms protecting these rights”

Family First have also preferenced Matthew Guy last in his safe Liberal seat of Bulleen. The party’s state leader, Moira Deeming, was disendorsed as a Liberal candidate after alleging Guy had placed her in a headlock earlier this year. Deeming later conceded she misunderstood the technical meaning of “headlock”.

articles.title: Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as traffic exhaust, study suggests
articles.summary:
Research finds highest levels of cancer-related PAH pollutants in cities that have widespread wood heating

Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to…

blocks.text: Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust, suggests new research across six European towns and cities.

Scientists measured the air in buildings where children spend much of their time; in schools, sports centres and homes. Specifically, they looked at polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), a family of pollutants that are given off when fuels are burned.

Dr Barend van Drooge, from Barcelona’s Institute for Environmental Assessment and Water Research (IEAWR) and senior author of the study, said: “Some of these compounds are related to cancers after prolonged exposures, as recognised by the International Agency for Cancer Research, and evidence exists that they delay cognitive development.”
Measurements were made in and around Athens, Barcelona, Colchester, Copenhagen, Helsinki and Lisbon.
Van Drooge continued: “Urban areas with wood-burning, such as Colchester and Athens, had the highest PAHs levels. Barcelona and Lisbon, where wood-burning is not practised, had the lowest levels.”
In Colchester and Athens, PAH exposure was greater than the World Health Organization guidelines.

Maria Antonia Aretaki, of the IEAWR in Barcelona and first author of the study, said: “Understanding the pollutants in children’s everyday surroundings is an important step towards protecting their health. Children are particularly important given their vulnerability to environmental pollutants and the potential health implications from exposure during childhood.”

Sports centres had the lowest concentrations. This was followed by schools, through some, especially those in Lisbon, were affected by nearby busy roads. Ventilation and indoor sources were important, but the homes with some of the greatest PAH were in areas with wood-burning, and many had open fireplaces and stoves.
Winter PAH concentrations were greater than summer.

The researchers divided the PAH into two types, according to molecular weight. In the Colchester homes, the high-molecular-weight PAH in winter were more than 10 times those in summer. The low-molecular-weight PAH were around three times greater.

Van Drooge continued: “Wood-burning is known to be an important emitter of PAH, but it was surprising that it has become such an important contributor to the overall presence of PAHs in urban areas. However, none of the cities exceeded unacceptable limits for lifetime cancer risk.”

Within the UK, the impacts of wood-burning are unlikely to unique to Colchester. Separate analysis of energy performance certificates by researchers at University College London showed that Colchester ranked 120th out of 333 local councils for density of wood burners per square kilometre. Worthing, Norwich and Reading all had around four times more.

A wintertime study of 53 children from two primary schools in Anglesey (Ynys Môn) found that children living in homes with wood burners could be exposed to over three times more particle pollution than those in non-wood-burning homes. The Anglesey study also found that homes had more air pollution than schools.

In Greece, wood-burning increased during the financial crisis that began in 2008. The cost of heating oil soared and many people turned to wood heating. This contributed to increased deaths associated with particle pollution in Athens, especially for those aged over 70. In some Greek towns, wood-burning leads to PAH that are 100 times greater in winter compared with summer.

articles.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize
articles.summary:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row…

blocks.text: A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.

In a written message from Vakilabad prison in north-eastern Iran, he said: “I accept this award in the name of all those who, for the ‘crime’ of aspiring to a free Iran, have been imprisoned, tortured, threatened, or sentenced to death; in the name of my comrades in the resistance units and the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives.”
He added: “The regime demands repentance, televised confessions and surrender from us. But our answer is clear: ‘We will never surrender; we will never submit to humiliation.’”

blocks.caption: Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani: ‘We will never surrender; we will never submit to humiliation.’ Photograph: Iran Human Rights

blocks.text: Vafaei Sani, 31, was arrested in 2020 for taking part in nationwide democracy protests in 2019 and accused of supporting an opposition group, the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK).

He was convicted of “corruption on Earth” and sentenced to death for a third time in September 2024 after “a grossly unfair trial”, according to Amnesty International. The supreme court upheld his death sentence on 4 October 2025. Since his arrest he has been tortured and held in solitary confinement for extended periods.

His continued imprisonment has drawn widespread international condemnation from prominent sportspeople, human rights organisations and legal experts who have called for his immediate release and the annulment of his death sentence.

The Magnitsky awards are named after the Russian lawyer, Sergei Magnitsky, who died in Russian police custody after exposing government corruption. They began in 2015 as a way to recognise journalists, politicians and activists in the field of human rights.

Sir William Browder, head of the Magnitsky Justice Foundation and the chair of the awards committee, said Vafaei Sani’s case was emblematic of the plight of many Iranians who face execution for standing against the regime. “Most important, Mohammad Javad is still alive,” he said. “That is why this award matters. Every time the world pays attention, it becomes harder to kill him quietly.”

blocks.caption: The awards are named after lawyer Sergei Magnitsky, who died in Russian police custody. Photograph: Alexander Zemlianichenko/AP

blocks.text: According to the Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights, at least 710 people have been executed in Iran since the beginning of 2026, including 79 political and religious prisoners.

In an October report, the organisation documented at least 106 death sentences against January protest detainees, 35 of whom had already been executed. In Vakilabad prison, where Vafaei Sani is detained, five people have been executed linked to the protests and 15 others are facing death sentences.

Vafaei Sani’s award comes at a time when there are growing fears for imprisoned Iranian athletes, who are considered role models in the country. Zohreh Abdollahkhani, founder of Human Rights for Sport, said: “The situation is really dire … We have seven athletes at risk of execution now, including Vafaei Sani.”

Ali-Sina Mostafavi, a mountaineer, was executed on 14 October after the anti-government protests. His death followed the killing of Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi, a taekwondo athlete, earlier that month, and the mixed martial arts fighter Gholamreza Khani Shakarab, who was hanged in May.

Abdollahkhani said people had been celebrating Vafaei Sani’s award. “Even people who don’t support his political view are supporting him to be heard,” she said. “I find it very inspiring that different political groups are coming together to say no to execution.”

In his message, Vafaei Sani said he wanted “a free and democratic Iran … where the people vote freely, women and men are equal, there is no discrimination on the basis of ethnicity, religion or belief, and no one is imprisoned or executed for political opposition”.
He added: “I remain steadfast in my pledge, and I will not bow before oppression until the people of Iran are free.”

articles.title: Students stage walkout vs. Trump visit, Pax Silica: 'We fight for our future'
articles.summary: Student groups from different universities staged campus walkouts on Friday to protest the upcoming visit of US President Donald Trump for the ASEAN 2026 Summit and the America-led Pax Silica…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 1:58pm

Student groups from different universities staged campus walkouts on Friday to protest the upcoming visit of US President Donald Trump for the ASEAN 2026 Summit and the America-led Pax Silica initiative.
At the University of the Philippines (UP) Diliman, students staged a campus walkout and rally to voice their indignation during what is called the National Youth Day of Action.

In a video report by Ian Cruz from UP Diliman, Kabataan Partylist Representative Renee Co called Trump a "rapist, pedophile, warmonger" who used the world's resources to pursue war for the benefit of his friends and artificial intelligence industries. She also slammed alleged plans to set up AI data centers into the Philippines.

"We don't want to sell the future of the youth. That's why behind me are the Gen Z of the Philippines, who stand in solidarity with the Gen Z of the world. We fight for our future and Donald Trump is not a part of this picture," Co said in a mix of English and Filipino.

In Ateneo de Manila University, students and university personnel also staged a walkout, according to student publication The GUIDON. Many protesters were seen carrying signs to reject the Pax Silica initiative and to protect the environment.

Students from the Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP) also held a mass walkout. Bayan Muna Partylist shared that their student chapter had joined the national protest action to reject Trump and Pax Silica.

"Mariing tinutulan ng mga kabataan ang Pax Silica na may kaugnayan sa estratehiya ng US sa critical minerals at semiconductor supply chains. Nananawagan ang Iskolar ng Bayan ilantad sa publiko ang buong nilalaman ng kasunduan at tiyaking mapangangalagaan ang pambansang interes," Bayan Muna said in Facebook post.

(The youth strongly reject Pax Silica, which is connected to the US' strategy regarding critical minerals and semiconductor supply chains. The Scholars of the Nation are calling for transparency to the public on the full contents of the agreement and to ensure national interests.)
Several other student groups have announced protest activities later in the day and in the days leading up to the ASEAN Summit.
The Pax Silica initiative, which is set for construction in New Clark City in Tarlac, has been the subject of controversy for several months.

Multi-sectoral groups have raised concerns over its possible impact to the environment due to its high energy and water consumption, and the potential displacement of indigenous people from their ancestral lands.

Earlier this week, the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) reiterated that Pax Silica in New Clark City will be governed by Philippine laws. The BCDA also previously clarified that the Pax Silica hub is not envisioned as a cluster of hyperscale data centers, but as an industrial hub that would include the manufacturing of semiconductors and microchips used in computers, laptops, electric vehicles, and other technologies. — VDV, GMA News

blocks.text: This marks the first state visit of a Brazilian president to the Philippines

MANILA, Philippines – Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva arrived in Manila on Friday, November 13, for a state visit ahead of his participation in the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.
Lula, the first Brazilian president to conduct a state visit to the Philippines, was accompanied by First Lady Rosāngela Lula Da Silva and his official delegation.
Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon, representing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., received Lula.
Before he got in his vehicle, Lula paused to watch the cultural performance in honor of his arrival.

On November 14, Saturday, Lula will begin his state visit with a wreath-laying ceremony at the Rizal Monument in Manila before heading to the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), the official venue of the ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

The Bazilian leader will have a téte-a-téte with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in the Private Office of the Delegation Building at the PICC before joining their respective officials for an expanded bilateral meeting.
After the meeting, the two leaders will witness the presentation of signed bilateral agreements and will have a joint press statement.

Lula, as guest of the chair, will join other leaders at the ASEAN Summit, which will take place from November 15 to 17. He first attended the ASEAN Summit, also as guest of the chair, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, last year.
Lula’s Manila visit comes just weeks after he won an unprecedented fourth term, and coincides with the 80th year of Philippines-Brazil relations. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte held dollar accounts, BPI confirms
articles.summary: The Vice President and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte also has two time deposit accounts in BPI's Julia Vargas branch

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte waves to supporters as she arrives at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court for the arraignment of her grave threats case, on October 9, 2026.
Noel Celis/Reuters
The Vice President and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte also has two time deposit accounts in BPI's Julia Vargas branch

MANILA, Philippines — The Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) has confirmed that Vice President Sara Duterte held US dollar accounts with the bank, according to a letter submitted to the Senate impeachment court.

The confirmation was brought up on Day 43 of Duterte’s impeachment trial on Thursday, November 12, after defense counsel Michael Poa manifested that the defense would no longer present BPI vice president and legal department Head Paul Roderick Ysmael as a witness.

Poa explained that Ysmael was initially intended to testify and authenticate a letter he sent to the BPI dated February 24, inquiring on the existence of the BPI accounts of the Vice President and her father, former president Rodrigo Duterte.
But since Poa had already testified on the letter in a previous hearing, the defense had opted to dispense with Ysmael’s testimony.

blocks.caption: Sara Duterte held dollar accounts, BPI confirms

blocks.text: House private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih said the prosecution had intended to cross-examine Ysmael and question some of the documents covered by the court’s subpoena, including “one letter coming from the BPI where it confirmed that the VP had dollar accounts.”

“This was not within our visibility because the subpoena issued previously did not include dollar accounts, and that was precisely one of the points that, if allowed, would have been part of our cross-examination,” Alih said during the trial on Thursday.
Impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said the court would have to respect the defense’s decision on which witnesses to present.

“At the proper time, Atty. Alih, you can make a tender, if at all, of excluded or not included evidence. This may be the proper subject matter of any memoranda you will submit or closing remarks of the counsel, whoever will make those closing remarks, at the end of the presentation of evidence from both sides,” Escudero said.
“Finally, this can be the proper subject matter of any rebuttal evidence you may wish to present after the respondent shall have rested, should you decide to do so,” he added.

House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro echoed Escudero’s remarks on Friday, November 13, saying the prosecution had already rested its case and could only cross-examine the document if the defense presented it as part of its evidence-in-chief.

“We are ready to conduct our cross-examination, but of course, we understand that during the deliberation on the validity of the issuance of subpoena to BIR, banks, AMLC, the presiding officer expressly excluded the foreign accounts in view of the confidentiality provisions,” Luistro said.

During its presentation of evidence, the prosecution presented records of two time deposit accounts held by the Vice President and her father at BPI’s Julia Vargas branch to establish an alleged “pattern of concealment” involving the Dutertes’ year-end bank balances.

However, the court has yet to subpoena the underlying records of the alleged dollar accounts, as impeachment proceedings are not expressly exempted from laws protecting foreign currency deposits. – Rappler.com

articles.title: More than 60% of Germany’s female soldiers report harassment or abuse
articles.summary:
Defence minister says extent of sexual misconduct found by study is ‘unacceptable’, as military tries to attract more recruits

Germany’s defence minister has promised a “zero tolerance”…

blocks.text: Germany’s defence minister has promised a “zero tolerance” approach to sexual abuse in the armed forces after a study found soldiers, particularly women, faced extensive harassment within the ranks.

The first comprehensive study of its kind into the Bundeswehr, conducted by the Centre for Military History and Social Sciences in Potsdam and released this week, comes as the military is trying to attract new recruits in response to global threats.

It found that more than 60% of female soldiers had reported experiencing some form of sexual harassment or abuse while on duty, ranging from sexually explicit remarks and degrading rituals to sexual violence.

Nearly 40% of the 4,000 women who responded to the survey said they had been addressed with suggestive comments and sexualised remarks, while 15% reported being harassed with mobile phone pictures taken against their will and in some cases altered using AI.
Just over 8% reported having been physically attacked, and 2% said they had been the victims of sexual violence.
Around 19% of male ‌soldiers had experienced a similar form of sexual misconduct, with non-binary or gay soldiers disproportionately affected, the study found.

Boris Pistorius, the defence minister, said the figures were “unacceptable”, in particular for a military that is trying to considerably increase its numbers. The Bundeswehr has pumped billions into boosting both personnel and equipment. Military bosses have set a target of 260,000 active-duty troops and 200,000 reservists by 2035, in the hope of avoiding the introduction of conscription.

Pistorius said he was struck by the finding that women in units with a higher proportion of other women were less frequently affected, which he said “argues in favour of recruiting more women into the Bundeswehr”.

He said he had been advised by some colleagues to ditch the study, over fears it would sully the reputation of the military. To do so, he said, would be akin to “turning a blind eye”, which in the long term would do more damage to the Bundeswehr. The study would be repeated every year, he added.
“Zero tolerance applies to sexual harassment within the Bundeswehr,” the minister said.

Pistorius expressed concern over a high level of reluctance to report incidents. About a third of those surveyed said they did not or would not report incidents because of a lack of trust in what their superiors would do.
after newsletter promotion
Before the study results were made public, Pistorius set up a hotline this month, meant to serve military personnel, which is to be staffed around the clock, and is called HELP.

In future, Pistorius said, those who made complaints should receive more information about the status of their proceedings, after victims said they were often left in the dark, but expected to continue serving.

The ministry said that, of 45,000 active or former members of the armed forces contacted to participate in the survey, 18% responded. It said its analysis showed that the figures were nevertheless representative.

articles.title: Court issues arrest warrant vs Quiboloy, others over US extradition request
articles.summary: Quiboloy and two others have been on the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s most wanted list since 2022

blocks.text: QUIBOLOY. Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC) Pastor Apollo Quiboloy arrives at the Senate to attend the public inquiry into the reported cases of abuse in KOJC, on October 23, 2024.
Senate Social Media Unit
Quiboloy and two others have been on the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s most wanted list since 2022

MANILA, Philippines – Makati City Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 145 has issued a warrant of arrest against doomsday preacher and Kingdom of Jesus Christ founder Apollo Quiboloy and two others in relation to the United States government’s request to extradite them.

“On 12 November 2026, pursuant to Section 4, Rule 2 of the Rules on Extradition Proceedings, the court issued an Extradition Warrant of Arrest against the [said] individuals, after finding probable cause that: (a) each extradite is the person named in the corresponding foreign arrest warrant and indictment, (b) that the offenses charged are extraditable offenses, and (c) that each extraditee committed the offense or offenses charged,” the Department of Justice (DOJ) said on Friday, November 13.
Apart from Quiboloy, the extradition petition includes Teresita Tolibas Dandan and Helen Panilag.
“At the same time, said court likewise issued a hold departure order against each extraditee, to prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines,” the DOJ added.

On November 10, the DOJ announced that the US request to extradite Quiboloy, Dandan, and Panilag was filed with the Makati City court the day before. The extradition petition was docketed as case number R-MKT-26-02823-SP and was raffled to Branch 145.

“Per the Rules on Extradition Proceedings, once the court is notified of the implementation of the arrest of the extraditee/s, the corresponding summons, together with a copy of the Petition and its annexes, shall be personally served on the extraditee/s, who shall then have a period of fifteen (15) days, from receipt of the summons, to file a verified Answer,” the DOJ explained.

After a review, the court will grant the petition if a prima facie case exists. Prima facie, as stated in Wa-acon vs. People, is a situation where evidence “is not rebutted or contradicted, making it good and sufficient on its face to establish a fact constituting a party’s claim or defense.”

Quiboloy, a close ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, is facing cases for international human trafficking, sex trafficking, conspiracy, and bulk cash smuggling. He has been detained in the Pasig City Jail since November 2024.
In local courts, he is facing a trafficking case in Pasig City, and separate cases of sexual abuse of a minor and child abuse in a Quezon City.
Quiboloy was arrested on September 8, 2024, in a raid led by former Philippine National Police chief Nicolas Torre III, after months of manhunt and tension in his home turf Davao City.
Quiboloy, Dandan, and Panilag have been on the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s most wanted list since 2022. There are also pending US warrants against them, which the DOJ said remain valid.
If the court grants the extradition request, Quiboloy and associates will be flown to the US, where they will face their charges. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

JAKARTA, Indonesia – Indonesia’s Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka handed his resignation to parliament’s upper house on Thursday, November 12, ending days of speculation about his political future, while his father, former President Joko Widodo, voiced support for current leader Prabowo Subianto.

The expression of support after the departure of Gibran, Indonesia’s highest-profile resignation since that of President Suharto in 1998, could ease signs of strain in the political alliance of Prabowo and predecessor Widodo.

“We will continue to support President Prabowo’s administration, especially programmes that serve the interests of the broader public,” the highly popular Widodo, known as Jokowi, told reporters outside his home in Solo in central Java.

Gibran’s resignation follows scrutiny over Prabowo’s signature political programs and doubts about the government’s ability to manage Southeast Asia’s biggest economy, where the political turmoil has sapped investor sentiment.
The rupiah weakened as much as 0.6% on Thursday to a fresh record low of 18,255 against the dollar.
Flanked by Gibran and parliamentarians, Prabowo said on Thursday he had accepted his deputy’s resignation with a “heavy heart” and praised Gibran’s contributions to the government.
“I felt assisted. He did his job well,” Prabowo said in a speech, citing Gibran’s work across Indonesian regions and his former deputy’s “chivalrous attitude.”
Gibran bowed and hugged Prabowo after the speech.

The rift between Prabowo and Jokowi, who twice defeated the powerful former general for the presidency before lending him his support in the face of term limits, had looked set to further destabilise the government, analysts said.

Gibran, 39, was elected alongside Prabowo in the 2024 election, during which Jokowi was accused of meddling in the process by influencing a court decision that changed the election rules, enabling Gibran to stand.
His resignation followed a push by lawmakers for Gibran’s impeachment on grounds of inadequate educational credentials.

It also followed rulings by the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court that his overseas high school qualifications fell short of legal requirements for vice presidential candidates, and had been wrongly accepted by election authorities.

In a video address late on Thursday, Gibran thanked Prabowo for his trust and said his resignation was his personal decision and unrelated to issues pertaining to his academic credentials, claiming his educational documents were complete.

“This decision to step down is also not a declaration of inability. Rather, it is a major step that I must take to preserve the government’s capacity to move forward further,” he said, adding that “democracy needs to be managed better.”
Parliamentary leaders will now gather to discuss the next steps, said Ahmad Muzani, speaker of the upper house.

The upper house will have to hold a session to declare a vacancy after Gibran’s resignation, while sending the president a letter seeking the names of two replacement candidates, senior law minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra said.
An upper house election will follow within 60 days.

Analysts said another sign of the gulf between Prabowo and Jokowi was last week’s revelation of an inquiry into illegal wiretapping by senior police officials, including former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo, widely seen as a Jokowi loyalist.
On Thursday, police said they had enough initial evidence to pursue treason charges against four suspects for wiretapping Prabowo, other politicians, activists and journalists.

At a hearing, lawmakers urged police chief Suyudi Ario Seto to uncover who ultimately ordered Listyo to conduct the alleged wiretapping, and the political interests that could be behind it. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ‘Looks like we’ll have to talk to people’: Australia sent back to time before email with major Microsoft outage
articles.summary: Government services and schools impacted by Outlook and Teams issue as company says fix not ‘taking as expected’
articles.byline: Jordyn Beazley, Josh Taylor, Adeshola Ore, Achol Arok and Josh Butler

blocks.text: Australian schools, courts and government services have been hurled back in time to how business used to be done after a global Microsoft outage caused emails and online meetings to go dark.

Australians began reporting issues with Microsoft 365 – which includes Outlook and Teams – just before 5am AEST on Friday, according to Down Detector. The problem appeared to peak at 9.22am with more than 5,500 reports of problems, including trouble opening and sending emails, before reports began to dip.

A Microsoft spokesperson said the company “had no indication of a cyber-attack” and suggested the issue could be related to a configuration change to its servers that was causing some to become overloaded and taken offline.
In an update to its website on Friday afternoon, the company said efforts to fix the issue were not “taking as expected”.
Government services affected

Service NSW, the one-stop shop agency for residents, drivers, and business owners to access government services, encouraged customers to delay their visits to its service centres. The agency put in place a priority callback system for those unable to complete urgent transactions during the outage.

“Some transactions in Service Centres and Call Centres are unavailable at this time,” it said. “Customers are encouraged to delay their visit to a Service Centre and to complete transactions online, where possible.”

Earlier in the morning, the federal home affairs minister, Tony Burke, appeared at a press conference with the Australian federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, and the Asio director general, Mike Burgess. Both said their systems had been affected by the outage, but they provided no further details.
Burgess said the spy agency’s systems “operate on multiple levels”, adding that they had been affected “on one level, yes, but not completely”.
The Australian Medical Association (AMA) said it had received reports that some hospitals and health clinics were experiencing clerical issues, but there had been no impacts to patient care.

“We’ve had some facilities return to using paper for scripts because authentication to get into lots of prescribing software requires multifactor verification, which requires you to be able to access your Microsoft-supported email,” the AMA president, Dr Michael Bonning, said.
“We don’t use any of these things for direct patient care. It’s always the authorisation in systems, so we’ve always got workarounds for that.”
Schoolbytes, a cloud-based administration platform used by schools in NSW, was “temporarily” unable to access emails due to the outage.

A text sent to a parent regarding the platforms outage said: “If you emailed the school after 3.15pm yesterday, or need to communicate with us regarding absences or changes to routines please call the office …”
Courts in South Australia and Victoria reported that the outage was affecting its email system. Victoria’s county court said its scheduled hearings were expected to go ahead as planned.
On social media, people shared how the outage was affecting their workday.
One Brisbane-based person posted on LinkedIn: “It’s all SMS and phone calls today … looks like we will have to talk to people while Microsoft sort out their email issues!”
after newsletter promotion
On Reddit, some users reported that while Outlook emails were down they could still access Microsoft’s workplace messaging platform, Teams.
“They could have taken Teams out with them so I’d be able to … just sit here and do absolutely nothing,” one Reddit user wrote.
Scam warning amid outage

Some services remained unaffected by the outage. The two major supermarkets – Coles and Woolworths – were operating as normal inside their stores. However, Coles said its internal email system has been affected.
The National Broadband Network said it was monitoring the outage, but remained unaffected.

The National Cyber Security Coordinator warned cybercriminals often seek to take advantage of the “uncertainty around these types of disruptions” with scam emails, texts, calls or social media messages.

“I encourage every Australian to remain vigilant and be cautious of unsolicited contact. Do not click on unexpected links, open attachments, or provide personal information. If you’re unsure, hang up and call back,” the coordinator wrote on social media.

Mark Gregory, an associate professor in the School of Engineering at RMIT University, said the outage appeared to be affecting the network layer in Microsoft’s systems, and was potentially similar to the configuration issue which brought down Optus’s network in 2023.
He said when some of the servers have configuration issues, it means customers are forced to share a smaller pool of servers to access the cloud services.
“If you lose part of that pool, then all of the users are trying to access the remaining servers, and that overloads them. And then they go down.
“And so you end up with a cascading problem. Then it takes time to find the underlying problem: in this case, a misconfiguration in the network layer.”
