articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon bought sim card under pseudonym a month before alleged murders, trial hears
articles.summary:
Former police officer tells court he bought sim card under name ‘Bob Ballard’ because he planned to go to media about alleged bullying from sergeant

Beau Lamarre-Condon has told a Sydney…

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon has told a Sydney court he obtained a sim card under a pseudonym a month before allegedly murdering two men because he wanted to go to the media about bullying allegations in the police force.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Sat in the witness box for the seventh day, Lamarre-Condon was asked about purchasing a sim card under the name “Bob Ballard” on 15 January 2024, about a month before the shootings.
Lamarre-Condon told the jury in his double murder trial it had “nothing to do with Jesse Baird”.
He was attempting to compile statements about “bullying from a certain sergeant” but was worried about speaking publicly on the issue, Lamarre-Condon said.
“I was wanting to go and compile all these statements and go to the media,” he told the New South Wales supreme court on Friday.
“I didn’t want to communicate at all from my phone because you can become a target … there would be repercussions.”
Under cross-examination by the crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC, Lamarre-Condon agreed he was using the new sim card to contact former and current officers.

But asked why his phone records showed he only contacted one police officer on this sim, Lamarre-Condon said it only revealed his normal phone calls, telling the court: “You can’t see what I did on Signal.”

The prosecutor said he could have used encrypted messaging app Signal on his normal phone, but Lamarre-Condon claimed police could make him unlock his own device and view his Signal records if he was investigated for talking to the media.
Hatfield also questioned why Lamarre-Condon had Davies’s contact details on his phone.
after newsletter promotion
The former officer claimed Davies’s details were on his Instagram.
“I went and blocked numerous Instagram [accounts] from my own Instagram because of this incident,” he said, referring to the shootings.
“I even blocked Jesse’s family members from my account. I didn’t want any of that.”
He deactivated his social media accounts soon after.
The trial before Justice Natalie Adams continues.

articles.title: Indigenous women leaders say budget doesn't address their realities
articles.summary: Indigenous leaders from across Canada gathered in Ottawa on Thursday to say Prime Minister Mark Carney’s new budget leaves Indigenous women out of the decisions made in the more than 500-page…

image.caption: President of the Native Women's Association of Canada Josie Nepinak, centre, speaks to reporters on Parliament Hill alongside, from left to right, Rose Mary Cooper of Pauktuutit Inuit Women of Canada, Les Femmes Michif Otipemisiwak director of intergovernmental relations Lisa Pigeau, Femmes Autochto

blocks.text: Politics·New

Indigenous leaders from across Canada gathered in Ottawa on Thursday to say Prime Minister Mark Carney’s new budget leaves Indigenous women out of the decisions made in the more than 500-page document.
Advocates point to lack of reference to Inuit women in budget

Indigenous leaders from across Canada gathered in Ottawa on Thursday to say Prime Minister Mark Carney's new budget leaves Indigenous women out of the decisions made in the more than 500-page document.
"Budget 2026 represents a missed opportunity to make Indigenous women's safety and healing a sustained national priority," said Josie Nepinak, president of the Native Women's Association of Canada.

She was joined by Lisa Pigeau, director of intergovernmental relations for Les Femmes Michif Otipemisiwak, former executive director of Pauktuutit Inuit Women of Canada Rose Mary Cooper, Quebec Native Women President Marjolaine Étienne and Ontario Native Women's Association CEO Cora McGuire-Cyrette.
Cooper said the budget does not account for the dangers Indigenous women face in northern and remote Indigenous communities, adding that Inuit women were not mentioned once in the document.

items: Carney government pledges $50B over 10 years for Indigenous programs, services
Carney's 2nd budget earmarks billions for affordability and Canadian sovereignty

blocks.text: "For many Indigenous women, safety is a plane ride away," Cooper said, adding that most communities in Inuit Nunangat can only be reached by air, and 60 per cent have no shelters or other safe spaces.

One in six Indigenous women have experienced at least one form of intimate partner violence, according to Statistics Canada. According to federal data, while Indigenous women make up only five per cent of all women in Canada, they made up approximately 26 per cent of women killed by an intimate partner in 2022.

"When an Indigenous woman needs to flee violence, she often must leave her family, her language, her land and her whole surrounding," Cooper said. "A model designed for seven cities does not work in small flying communities where food and housing costs weigh much more. One size does not fit all."
Cooper added that responses "must be tailored to where Indigenous women live and be designed and led by the women who live there."

While Carney's budget pledges $50 billion over the next 10 years to Indigenous programs and services — including $32 billion over 10 years for First Nations housing and infrastructure — many Inuit and Métis groups have expressed concerns over their asks not being met in this year's proposed spending.

items: Federal budget's lack of Métis-specific funding concerns Métis leaders
Infrastructure gap and specific claims top issues for Assembly of First Nations for federal budget

blocks.text: Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami (ITK) told CBC News in a statement earlier this week that while it welcomes the budget's promise of $575 million over five years to fund the Inuit Child First Initiative and transition to the new Inuit-led initiative Pirutsiagutiit, it was "disappointed" by the lack of specific references to Inuit in other areas of the document.

Métis leaders were also concerned earlier this week with the budget's lack of Métis-specific funding, with the word "Métis" only appearing once in the document. Manitoba Métis Federation (MMF) President David Chartrand said he was "appalled" by the absence of distinct funding for Métis.

During Thursday's news conference, the leaders also raised concerns about the government's plan to end homelessness in 10 years. McGuire-Cyrette said this will not be achieved "unless the government works with the agencies on the ground."

items: Carney's new budget aims to end homelessness in 10 years

blocks.text: Citing a 2024 Ontario Native Women's Association study that 83 per cent of Indigenous women live off reserve in rural and urban centres, she said "the budget is silent for the majority of urban Indigenous agencies" with the majority of investments are going to on-reserve services.
"If we're not at the table, how can you work with us?" she said.
Funding welcome, gaps remain

One significant provision from this year's budget for Indigenous women was providing $3.6 million to renew the Red Dress Alert pilot, which was developed with Indigenous partners to address the crisis of missing and murdered Indigenous women and girls in Canada (MMIWG).
Nepinak said that while she welcomes the funding and believes it will save lives, it "doesn't fix or address all of the gaps that continue to exist" in safety and protections for Indigenous women.
McGuire-Cyrette added that the investments in the pilot were nice to see, but are for the "aftermath of violence" against Indigenous women, girls and two-spirit people as opposed to prevention.
"We're not seeing those upstream investments," McGuire-Cyrette said.
Cooper added that for Inuit women living in Inuit Nunangat, "the needs are greater and reflecting what those needs are will be important" on how the pilot rolls out.

Pigeau said that while the leaders have not requested a meeting with Minister of Crown-Indigenous Relations Rebecca Alty since the budget's tabling last week, they spoke with her before the budget release and look forward to meeting with "all ministers that would be involved" because it's "beyond just one issue."
"It's a multi-systemic approach that is needed to address the gender and orientation-based violence that faces Indigenous women," Pigeau said.

Nepinak added that the leaders brought up the need for supports and investments for Indigenous women's lives in Ottawa in a February conference that Alty attended, but "it feels like it fell on deaf ears."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Sophia Laporte is an intern with CBC's Parliamentary Bureau in Ottawa and a fourth-year journalism and humanities student at Carleton University.

articles.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
articles.summary: The army has taken control of most of Tigray's main towns - it is unclear if the TPLF is capable of fighting back.

blocks.text: Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment.

"People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC.
After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter.
"Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion.
Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next."

Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force.
Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements.

Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority.
Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat.

"The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage."

Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says.
Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost.
Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC.

He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy."

The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability.
It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored.
Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes.
Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days.

"We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active.
Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents.
The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.

As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds.

Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded.

Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC.

Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations.
However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael.

Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF."

He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says.

Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says.

What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded."

While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours."

In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict.

"First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF."

Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade.

Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement.
In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters.
"If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says.

Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says.

Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government.

However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence.
In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace.
"Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle.

articles.title: Calls grow for release of beloved California nurse detained by ICE: ‘We want her home’
articles.summary:
Ann Lawani was taken from her home, sparking a huge outcry among students and faculty at her university

Nearly two months after ICE agents whisked a beloved California nurse and professor…

blocks.text: Nearly two months after ICE agents whisked a beloved California nurse and professor from her home in Lodi, her university has ramped up calls for her release.

“She needs to come home,” said Eileen Fry-Bowers, dean for the University of San Francisco’s nursing school,in reference to Ann Lawani, who was arrested by immigration agents in September and has since been shuffled between detention centers in California, Texas, and Louisiana, in a series of opaque transfers.
Lawani, 39, came to the US in 2007. She established herself as a nursing professional, obtaining a master’s and doctoral degree in the field, before stepping into academia.

She steers two programs at the University of San Francisco, one a master’s entry program geared toward students with non-nursing backgrounds and another a bachelor’s program for students seeking to work in public health safety-net institutions.
“She basically has her hands on almost 300 students that she engages with on a regular basis,” Fry-Bowers said.
Lawani’s detention has sparked outcry from local lawmakers, who have advocated on her behalf to ICE authorities, as well as her students and colleagues, who say her absence is deeply felt on campus.
One of those students, Casey Murray, a nursing science graduate student, described Lawani as a warm educator who could recall the first and last names of pupils she had not seen since orientation.

“We have 37 days left until we graduate,” Murray said. “She has supported us to the fullest extent up until the point that she was kidnapped. We want her at our graduation, and we want her home with her family.”

Federal immigration officials say Lawani entered the US on a visitor’s visa in 2007, which she overstayed. She was issued a final order of removal in August 2013, according to a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) spokesperson.
Natalia Santanna, Lawani’s lawyer, confirmed the removal order, but noted that DHS’s account was “incomplete”.

“Dr Lawani applied for asylum within one year of being in the United States. And, in the same 2013 order, the immigration judge found that Ann would more likely than not face persecution in Nigeria and granted withholding of removal,” Santanna said. “That is not a temporary stay. It is a continuing bar to removal to Nigeria. Dr Lawani has lived in the United States pursuant to that grant of withholding of removal since 2013.”
Santanna said they have filed a habeas petition to challenge the legality of her detainment, which remains pending in California’s eastern district court.
Meanwhile, Lawani’s students and colleagues are continuing to mobilize around her.

Lawani sent Fry-Bowers a text about being in ICE’s custody, shortly after her arrest. Fry-Bowers, who was on vacation, heard from another dean that Lawani had been absent from a meeting, which she described as out of character.
After the school heard from Lawani’s family, they jumped into action, aiding with legal representation and registering their alarm with the area’s congressional delegation.

In late October, Josh Harder, a congressman, who represents Lawani’s district, expressed his concerns about her case to DHS secretary Markwayne Mullin, among them the lack of notice before her arrest and her various whereabouts not being reflected in an online detainee database.

“Given her longstanding compliance, lack of criminal history, and substantial community ties, there is no apparent public safety justification for keeping her detained thousands of miles from home while her case proceeds,” Harder wrote then in a letter.
Fry-Bowers praised Lawani, citing her work with patients in hospice and palliative care.

“She cares for the most vulnerable, helps them maintain their dignity and comfort as they prepare for death,” she said. “She is a consummate professional. The highest praise I could ever give a nursing colleague is that I would want them taking care of my family member or myself, and she would be at the top of the list.”

articles.title: Pilot killed in Quebec Remembrance Day crash had lifelong passion for flying, friends say
articles.summary: Friends of Daniel Parent — the man killed in a plane crash during a Remembrance Day event in Saint-Georges-de-Beauce, Que., — are remembering him for being an excellent and experienced pilot.

image.caption: Daniel Parent is remembered by friends as having been a quiet and reserved man, with a deep passion for aviation. (Courtesy of Jean-Pierre Champagne Productions)

blocks.text: Montreal
Friends of Daniel Parent — the man killed in a plane crash during a Remembrance Day event in Saint-Georges-de-Beauce, Que., — are remembering him for being an excellent and experienced pilot.
Friends say Daniel Parent, 68, was an experienced pilot

Friends of Daniel Parent — the 68-year-old man killed in a plane crash during a Remembrance Day event in Saint-Georges-de-Beauce, Que., — are remembering him for being an excellent and experienced pilot.
“He was driven by an all-consuming passion for aviation,” Robert Bergeron, a fellow pilot and friend of Parent, told Radio-Canada.
“Daniel had been passionate about aviation for more than 40 years.”
He recalled a story from Parent's earlier days, when he landed a small two-seater Cessna 150 in his parents’ farm field near Saint-Honoré, Que.
“It caused quite a sensation,” Bergeron said.
It’s normal for young pilots to be a bit more daring and adventurous, Bergeron said, but Parent had grown into a mature man with nothing left to prove.
Robert Bergeron was presiding over Wednesday’s Remembrance Day ceremony in Saint-George on Wednesday for a local branch of the Royal Canadian Legion. (Radio-Canada)

Parent’s plane of choice eventually became the Mooney M20C, a high-performance aircraft designed for cross-country flying. According to the Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB), Parent had been flying a single-engine Mooney on Wednesday when he crashed.
Bergeron shared his admiration of Parent, who he said flew his Mooney plane across the continent, "as far away as Alaska, California and the Grand Canyon."
“He was an inspiration to me,” said Bergeron.
He said it was only after Parent had completed several of those journeys that he found the courage to follow in his footsteps.
“I always described him — and I told him this on several occasions — as my mentor.”

items: Pilot killed in plane crash during Remembrance Day event in Quebec's Beauce region

blocks.text: The Remembrance Day ceremony in Saint-Georges was one Parent had been part of for many years, according to Bergeron.

He was performing what's called a "Missing Man" formation, where one aircraft separates from the formation and gradually climbs into the sky to symbolize the departure of someone in the Armed Forces who has died in combat.
“The formation took off, and the formation came back without him," said Bergeron of what happened Wednesday. "It's an absolutely terrible tragedy.”
“It was an immense sadness for me to see him leave us this way."
'You only find out afterward,' recalls pilot
On Thursday, the TSB provided an update about what happened.

"During a formation flight of six aircraft performing for Remembrance Day commemorations, one of the aircraft, a single-engine Mooney, broke away from the formation as planned as part of their show and briefing," said TSB spokesperson Nic Defalco in a statement.
"When attempting to rejoin the formation, the aircraft passed beneath the other aircraft and continued on that trajectory, ultimately crashing into a wooded area."
The TSB continues to investigate the crash.
The pilots taking part in the ceremony were all part of the Club Aéronautique de Beauce, a local flight club. Hugues Drouin was among them.
He explains that due to the technical nature of the "Missing Man" formation, the pilots are highly concentrated on the aircraft that’s guiding them during the manoeuvre.
Hugues Drouin was a friend of Daniel Parent. (Radio-Canada)
So he didn’t immediately realize Parent’s plane had gone down.
“What happened,” he said, “was that everything was going well during the flight. And at one point the leader said, ‘Missing Man Go, Missing Man Go,’” in reference to the procedure.
“Then we heard Daniel say, ‘OK.’ And he left the formation.”
Drouin says Parent was supposed to return. But when the leader asked for confirmation of his position, there was no response.
“So we really couldn't know what had happened. Because it's not like driving a car, where you can look to the left or right. You only find out afterward.”
Drouin said he realized after the accident, while he was still in the air, that Parent's plane was no longer there.
It was after landing, and when getting out of his plane, that Drouin began to have a strong physical response. He said his legs wouldn’t hold him up.

“I imagine it's probably the same for someone who's been in a car accident or something like that,” he said. “In the moment, you don't really realize what's happening, and afterward you have significant physical and mental reactions.”
As Drouin continues to process the loss of his friend, he remembers Parent as being an excellent pilot.
“He was someone you could rely on,” said Drouin. “He was a very, very good person.”
Quebec pilot killed in crash linked to ceremony for Remembrance Day
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Patricia Kozicka is a digital journalist with CBC Montreal. She has previously worked in Toronto and Edmonton. You can reach her at patricia.kozicka@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Who could replace the departed Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO?
articles.summary:
Chief financial officer Colette Kress to take over on interim basis but other names are in mix to be permanent successor

The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week,…

blocks.text: The hunt is on for a new Nvidia CEO. It comes after a whirlwind week, which saw the company head and co-founder, Jensen Huang, resign amid multiple allegations of extramarital affairs, including one that involved an alleged Chinese spy and two with company employees.

Nvidia immediately named Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, as the interim CEO. It’s possible she could stay on permanently, but the company could also name another candidate for the full-time role. Names that have been floated include Ian Buck, who manages Nvidia’s AI hardware and software products, and Rene Haas, a former Nvidia employee and the current CEO of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker.

Whoever takes over from Huang will have tremendous sway in the burgeoning world of artificial intelligence. The entire AI ecosphere relies on Nvidia, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Nvidia is also a central driver of the US economy and one of the world’s most valuable companies, with a market cap of around $4tn.

Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, is known as an ambitious and visionary CEO who had a hand in most all aspects of the business. He led in an unusual management style, having about 60 direct reports, giving him more control over the company’s daily functions. His son and daughter also work at Nvidia, with his daughter seen as his possible proxy, but neither appear to have sufficient experience to take the helm.

Kress, 59, joined Nvidia in 2013 as the CFO after working in finance roles at Texas Instruments, Microsoft and Cisco. She’s a regular contributor to the company’s quarterly earnings calls, and has overseen Nvidia go from a niche firm geared toward video game chips to a trillion-dollar AI juggernaut.

“Colette has helped lead Nvidia through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Harvey C Jones, the newly named chair of Nvidia’s board of directors, said in a statement on Thursday. “The board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team.”

Kress wrote that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years”. She will serve as both the CEO and interim CFO until the board names a permanent successor.

The board said it was starting a search for Huang’s permanent replacement and is considering internal and external candidates. Along with Kress, Buck is seen as a possible successor. He has worked at Nvidia since 2004 and in charge of deploying generative AI in partnership with the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI and more.

Haas, the CEO of Arm Holdings, is also well-known at Nvidia, having worked there for seven years as a vice president and general manager before joining Arm in 2013. Lisa Su, the CEO of chipmaker AMD, is also being named as a possible replacement for Huang. Her company is Nvidia’s most direct and fierce competitor; she’s also a distant cousin to Huang.
Nvidia’s CEO turmoil comes as the company is set to report its third-quarter earnings next Tuesday.

articles.title: FIFA loses bid to block UEFA evidence gathering against Infantino
articles.summary: A New York judge has dismissed soccer governing body FIFA's attempts to shield its president from investigation. Europe's UEFA is seeking evidence of wrongdoing by Gianni Infantino.

image.caption: Infantino came under fire after details emerged of his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments to private investorsImage: Bassam Masoud/REUTERS

blocks.text: New York Federal Court Judge Jeannette Vargas on Thursday rejected a bid by US subsidiaries of soccer's global governing body FIFA to block Europe's governing body UEFA from gathering evidence tied to FIFA President Gianni Infantino's attempts to sell shares of the World Cup and other tournaments to private investors.

UEFA filed for discovery in the case in August with the intent of removing Infantino from office and has said it will file a criminal complaint against the embattled soccer boss in Switzerland if it finds evidence of financial wrongdoing.
UEFA is seeking discovery of evidence from Infantino's partners in the so-called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, a plan that instantly sparked fierce backlash when it became public in July.

The court's ruling means UEFA can now request the right to obtain documents tied to the deal from the US bank JP Morgan and the investment firm Thrive Capital, which is owned by Joshua Kushner — brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and son of US Ambassador to France Charles Kushner, a convicted felon whom Trump pardoned before appointing him to that post.

Two FIFA subsidiaries had sought to block UEFA's efforts, but Vargas ruled they had no "direct, substantial and legally protectable interest" in the case, which is specifically aimed at Infantino and his dealings.
"Nothing in this record indicates that the US FIFA parties, or even FIFA itself, will be parties in the contemplated criminal proceedings," according to Vargas.

In an eight-page ruling issued from the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, Vargas wrote, "Certainly the US FIFA parties have not alleged facts suggesting they would be defendants in such a proceeding."
FIFA lawyers countered by saying, "The court has not addressed the merits of UEFA's application and no documents are required to be produced."
FIFA accused of blackmail in exchange for Infantino support
What happened when Infantino unveiled his plan to set up the FFE?

Infantino came under intense fire for seeking to set up FFE to manage FIFA's commercial interests in the World Cup and other competitions by allowing private investors to purchase minority stakes, with three continental soccer confederations rejecting the plan and UEFA threatening to boycott future FIFA tournaments if the plan was not scrapped.
The 211 member federations of FIFA, which effectively own the Zurich, Switzerland-based not-for-profit outfit, were offered $20 million (€18.1 million) payments each to approve the project.
Infantino initially pushed back but was eventually forced to abandon the plan in August.

UEFA has continued to push for Infantino's ouster since then and has demanded answers about the details of his scheme, for instance, questions about how Thrive was selected to head the investor group.

In what is the biggest challenge Infantino has seen in his 11-year stint as head of FIFA, UEFA has filed requests for discovery in multiple states in an effort to ascertain whether there was wrongdoing on his part.

Infantino has been accused of seeking retribution against those opposed to his leadership and in September FIFA told a judge in Florida, where the governing body has offices in a Miami suburb, that UEFA's legal pursuits amount to harassment of Infantino.
Infantino has shown no sign that he is willing to vacate his post and instead plans to run for reelection as FIFA president.
To do so, he must pass an eligibility and integrity check conducted by a FIFA-appointed panel.
So far, only one person, Japan's Kohzo Tashima, a member of FIFA's 37-member ruling council since 2016, has declared his candidacy.

UEFA is expected to propose another challenger and is currently seeking to get FIFA Head of Global Development and former Arsenal London coach Arsene Wenger to stand against the Swiss incumbent, who is also his boss.
Anyone wishing to challenge Infantino must declare by next Wednesday, November 18.

blocks.caption: UEFA is trying to get Arsene Wenger (l) to challenge his boss Gianni Infantino (r) for FIFA's presidencyImage: Sebastian Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

articles.title: Second world war ‘brain’ bunker in cliffs of Dover opens to public
articles.summary:
Hidden bunker, entered via a hatch in a field, controlled a gun battery used to attack German ships in Channel

It has been kept secret for decades, buried four metres deep into the white…

blocks.text: It has been kept secret for decades, buried four metres deep into the white cliffs of Dover. But from Friday, members of the public will finally be able to visit a pioneering command bunker that was ordered by Winston Churchill and proved a vital defence during the second world war.

The Fan Bay plotting room, which is encased in concrete, housed the first land-based computer-aided targeting system. This acted as a “brain” for a gun battery that was used to defend Dover and attack German ships in the Channel, according to Jon Stewart, who led the excavation project for the National Trust.
Stewart was the first person to enter the bunker when it was rediscovered in 2017 after it had been secretly mothballed in 1957 and classified until 1981 owing to its military importance.

“It was a Tutankhamun moment for a conflict archaeologist,” he said. “We had done all this research on the people who had served there, and then suddenly you’re standing in their office. It was an exciting moment.”

blocks.caption: Visitors take a tour of the plotting room at Fan Bay. Photograph: John Miller/National Trust Images/John Miller

blocks.text: The plotting room and the artillery it controlled can be directly traced to Churchill. Soon after his “fight them on the beaches” speech, he visited the Kent coast and was alarmed to observe enemy ships passing through the strait of Dover unchallenged.
At the same time, Dover was on the frontline of a Britain facing regular bombardment by enemy guns in occupied France.
In a July 1940 memo Churchill wrote: “We have to fight for command of the straits by artillery, to destroy the enemy batteries and fortify our own.”

He ordered the most advanced technology to be used and demanded weekly updates on progress on Dover’s new defences. The guns were ready within 100 days and the plotting room bunker was completed 64 days later.
“The guns were known around here as Churchill’s pets,” Stewart said.

blocks.caption: 3D reconstruction of hidden World War II plotting room beneath White Cliffs of Dover

blocks.text: Physical traces of the urgency of the construction were still visible at the site, said Stewart. He pointed to the rough openings through the walls and floors for the cabling. Contemporary accounts describe how the equipment was installed before drawings governing its layout were available.

The plotting room housed a 1.8-metre-long electromechanical computer known as a fire direction table. It was used to calculate the position of moving ships when shells hit and to send firing instructions to gun crews.

Stewart said the discovery of the plotting room reminded him of the rescue of Bletchley Park, the codebreaking site in Buckinghamshire, in the 1990s. “We didn’t know about it then, but now it’s all part of our national consciousness,” he said. “The plotting room is a new hidden history.”

He added: “We tend to think of plotting tables as glamorous Wrens [members of the Women’s Royal Naval Service] pushing around markers on a map as they do in war films. But it’s not a map – it’s a really cutting edge electromechanical computer, and it is completely unique.”
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Winston Churchill views activity in the Channel from an observation post at Dover Castle in 1940. Photograph: Sean Carney/© Crown copyright IWM 003499

blocks.text: The computer was deliberately destroyed in 1957 to stop it falling into enemy hands.
Up to 10 people at a time worked in the plotting room. Stewart is keen to make contact with anyone who had family members who served there, to help him understand how the machine worked.
“What we know about it is based on a manual and ghost markings on the floor. I would really love to hear if anybody knows if their family members served at Fan Bay because the records are scant.”

The identities of only a handful of people who operated the computer are known. They include Wallas Eaton, an actor who later appeared as Senator Ludicrus Sextus in the TV comedy series Up Pompeii, alongside Frankie Howerd.

blocks.caption: This image of a battery plotting room interior shows how the Fan Bay bunker may have looked when it was operational.  Photograph: Major Barlow Archives

blocks.text: A man named WP Bryant, a lance bombardier, was also recorded as a plotter at Fan Bay. “He was a tailor so he probably had a head for numbers,” said Stewart.

The plotting room, which from Friday can be visited via National Trust guided tours through a hatch in a field, has been preserved as Stewart and his team found it. Remnants include old newspapers found on the floor, old shoes and official notices. There is also chalked graffiti on one of the service tunnels saying “heroes fan hole Dodds and Petitt”. Stewart said Dodds and Petitt may have been involved in installing cables to the bunker.
“They were probably self-appointed heroes responsible for marshalling horrible thick cable through particularly uncomfortable tunnels,” he said.

“There’s something very special about standing in a place that has changed so little since the people who worked here left. Rather than recreate the past, we’ve carefully conserved the plotting room so visitors can experience it much as we found it, with all the marks of its history still visible. It’s a rare opportunity to discover a completely different side of the white cliffs.”

articles.title: Fact check: Viral quote fabricates drug war victim's sister plea to leave Hague
articles.summary: No credible news report or public statement supports the supposed plea.

blocks.text: Headlines
November 13, 2026 | 8:00am
A viral quote card falsely attributes a plea to return to the Philippines to Sheerah Escudero, sister of a drug war victim.
Screenshot taken Nov. 12, 2026, 12:00 p.m.
MANILA, Philippines — A viral Facebook post falsely claims that the sister of a drug war victim pleaded to be brought home from The Hague after experiencing hardship in the Netherlands.

The quote card, shared by Facebook account Boss Bombay on Tuesday, November 10, attributes the supposed plea to Sheerah Escudero, whose brother Ephraim was killed in 2017 during the drug war of former President Rodrigo Duterte.
Facebook account Boss Bombay shared the viral quote card falsely attributing a plea to return to the Philippines to Sheerah Escudero in a post published on November 10, 2026.
The graphic features an image purportedly showing Escudero in tears, alongside the statement:
Tulungan nio kami Maka uwi Ng pinas hirap na kami Dito sa The Hague!
Rating: This is fake.
Facts
No credible news report or public statement from Escudero supports the claim that she pleaded to return to the Philippines because of difficulties in The Hague.
The quote card also bears no logo or other identifying marks linking it to a credible news organization or source.
A Google reverse image search yielded no earlier matches for the image purportedly showing Escudero in tears. The image's origin and authenticity could not be established.
Sheerah Escudero speaks at a gathering of families of drug war victims in Quezon City on April 25, 2026.

Escudero attended a gathering of families of drug war victims in Quezon City on April 25, following the International Criminal Court's (ICC) rejection of Duterte's appeal challenging the court's jurisdiction and the confirmation of all charges against the former president.
At the event, she vowed that the families would continue fighting for justice for the victims amid attacks against them.
"Patay na po ang mga kaanak natin. Sino pong titindig para sa kanila? Sino magtatanggol para sa sarili nila kundi po tayo mga naiwan nila?" Escudero said.
Sheerah Escudero condemns the circulation of edited photos of drug war victims’ relatives during Duterte’s confirmation of charges hearing in The Hague on February 26, 2026.
Previously, Escudero was among the relatives of drug war victims who traveled to The Hague for Duterte’s confirmation of charges hearing from February 23 to 27.
On February 26, she condemned the circulation of manipulated images depicting her and other victims' relatives supposedly carrying designer handbags.

“Wala na silang ibang ginagawa kung hindi i-manipulate ‘yung statements namin, ‘yung images po namin to discredit ‘yung totoong panawagan ng mga pamilya ng biktima, which is para ilatag ‘yung katotohanan at manawagan para sa hustisya,” she said.
("They do nothing but manipulate our statements and images to discredit the genuine call of victims' families, which is to present the truth and demand justice.")
Why we fact-checked this
The fabricated quote is part of a pattern of misleading social media content targeting relatives of drug war victims pursuing accountability before the ICC.

In February, multiple pro-Duterte Facebook pages circulated an edited photo of Rubilyn Litao of the group Rise Up for Life and for Rights, Llore Pasco and Escudero holding bags that appeared to be from Louis Vuitton and Moynat.
The latest quote card circulated ahead of the scheduled November 30 opening of Duterte's ICC trial over alleged crimes against humanity linked to his administration's war on drugs.
As of Nov. 12, the Facebook post had garnered more than 26,000 reactions, 8,000 comments and 1,700 shares.

articles.title: Russell Brand accused of misconduct by six more women, according to report
articles.summary:
Allegations of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour made against ex-comedian who was jailed on Monday

Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by a…

blocks.text: Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by a further six women, according to a report.
The comedian, 51, is accused of having sex with a woman without her consent and then apologising afterwards, an investigation by the Times and the Sunday Times said.
The newspapers also alleged the comedian continued having sex with another woman after she asked him to stop because he was hurting her.

Brand, 51, was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison on Monday after being convicted of raping a 21-year-old fan and sexually assaulting three women in separate incidents between 2004 and 2009. He was cleared of two further charges of rape and one of attempted indecent assault at Southwark crown court in London.
The Times reported that a woman said she had an on-off relationship with the actor in the late 2000s after a professional meeting at his London home.
On one occasion, she said they were in bed together when he moved to initiate sex. Having noticed he was not wearing a condom, she said she asked him to stop.

She told the Times: “And then he was very close, on top of me, and sort of pushing – but I knew he didn’t have a condom on and I said: ‘No, stop,’ and I started to sort of try and move. And … that wasn’t happening.”
The woman added she decided at that moment that “I’m not going to fight” because “who knows what he could do”.
After the alleged incident, she said Brand apologised to her in person and by text message. “I justified it in my head by saying to myself: at least he admitted it.”
Another woman who encountered Brand when she was queueing to meet him with a friend in 2007 aged 19 said she told him during sex: “It’s painful”, according to the report.
She alleged he would not stop, adding: “And then it gets worse and it’s really painful. And I say ‘stop’ and he doesn’t stop.”
The woman claimed he said afterwards: “Tonight was consensual. Nobody did anything they didn’t want to do.”

Brand is also accused of misconduct by a fan, then in her late 20s, who met him after he performed at The Chapel venue in San Francisco in 2013, who claimed he “manhandled” her and forced his hand down her trousers, telling the Times: “I didn’t resist. I just sort of let it happen.”
Another woman, then in her mid-twenties, said Brand approached her in 2005 at a music festival and told her: “Please I just need to have sex with you, I will pay you.”
According to the Times investigation, Brand is also accused of misconduct by a woman who was in her late 20s when she won a BBC 6 Music competition and was invited as a guest on his show in 2006.
after newsletter promotion

After seeing each other sporadically for the next year, she claimed the comedian told her to lick a toilet seat at his house and “got angry” when she refused, adding: “[He] seemed pissed off that I wouldn’t let him humiliate me.”
Another woman, who worked at a London venue Brand visited regularly in 2015, said a member of Brand’s staff told her there: “Russell wants you” and said: “He’s in the disabled toilets”.
She said when she went in the lights were off and Brand claimed he wanted toilet paper, but grabbed her when she went to hand it to him.

The new allegations could not be reported until his criminal case ended to avoid prejudicing proceedings. The Times reported that “extensive steps” were taken to corroborate the claims and that none of the sources were paid.

The newspapers reported that Brand was approached for comment via legal representatives after his conviction on Monday. His lawyer reportedly said he would consider “injunctive relief” but did not send any response to the allegations despite being given additional time and an agreed deadline passing. Brand has previously denied wrongdoing and claimed all his relationships were consensual.

The prime minister, Andy Burnham, has said the media industry needs to “look at itself” and “step forward” to protect women and girls following Brand’s rape conviction and allegations of sexual misconduct made against the comedian David Walliams in an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News.
Walliams has denied the allegations. Brand’s lawyer was contacted for comment.

articles.title: Christina Applegate asks if breast implants are behind symptoms after MS misdiagnosis
articles.summary: U.S. actor Christina Applegate is questioning whether her breast implants could be contributing to her pain and fatigue. Experts say symptoms associated with breast implant illness can overlap with…

image.caption: Christina Applegate attends an event in Santa Monica, Calif., in January 2020. On her MeSsy podcast with co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Applegate said she is investigating whether her breast implants could be contributing to her ongoing health issues. She recently revealed that doctors determined she do

blocks.text: Entertainment

U.S. actor Christina Applegate is questioning whether her breast implants could be contributing to her pain and fatigue. Experts say symptoms associated with breast implant illness can overlap with other conditions, so people experiencing them should seek a thorough medical evaluation before making decisions about their implants.
On her podcast, the actor questioned if her implants might be leaking and contributing to her health problems

Actor Christina Applegate, 54, says she is exploring whether her breast implants could be linked to her pain and fatigue after learning she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) — the diagnosis she received in 2021.

On the Nov. 10 episode of MeSsy, the podcast she co-hosts with actor Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Applegate, who first gained fame as a teen in the hit sitcom Married With Children, said someone had recently sent her a study describing breast implant-related symptoms as resembling MS.
"I swear, over the last five years or whatever, I thought, 'What if they're leaking and they're poisoning me?'" she said, noting she plans to discuss the possibility with her doctors.

items: As Christina Applegate reveals MS misdiagnosis, doctor warns of wrong treatment risks
The subject of Lyme disease is littered with misinformation. Celebrities are part of the problem, experts say

blocks.text: Applegate underwent a double mastectomy and breast reconstruction in 2008 after being diagnosed with an early form of breast cancer and testing positive for a BRCA1 gene mutation, which carries a higher risk of breast and other cancers. On her podcast, she said she was "way overdue" to have her implants replaced.

She has also described worsening pain and difficulty moving her right shoulder, saying it can take her at least 10 minutes to sit up and get out of bed. Those symptoms, she said, are overwhelming because "there's so many different things that could be going on."

Her search comes after doctors told her in October that she does not have MS. At the time, Applegate said the news left her back at "Square 1," her physical struggles have continued and she's undergoing testing for other possible explanations, including rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and Lyme disease.
While the cause of Applegate's symptoms remains unknown, breast implants have been associated with illness in some cases, though the condition is not well understood.
What is known about breast implant illness

Breast implant illness, or BII, is a term for symptoms reported by some people with implants, including fatigue, cognitive changes, joint pain and muscle pain. This photo shows a Biocell textured breast implant by Allergan. (Nicolas Amaya/CBC)
Breast implant illness, or BII, is a term for symptoms reported by some people with implants.
As of Dec. 31, 2025, Health Canada had received 663 reports of symptoms or diseases associated with breast implants — about one report for every 1,025 implants sold in Canada.

Fatigue was the most frequently reported symptom, followed by mood changes, gastrointestinal symptoms and cognitive changes. These are reports, not confirmed cases: Health Canada says the available information cannot establish whether implants caused the symptoms, which may have other causes.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) says BII is not a formal medical diagnosis and has no specific test. Reports of symptoms such as fatigue and joint problems cannot establish how often they occur or whether implants caused them.

Julie Elliott, a Canadian breast implant illness and implant-associated cancer advocate with the Breast Implant Safety Alliance who says she experienced health problems after breast augmentation, told CBC News that some symptoms reported by people with implants can overlap with MS symptoms.

items: National breast implant registry much needed but long overdue, patients and doctors say
Alberta women with breast implant illness urge doctors to warn others of risk

blocks.text: "Chronic fatigue, changes in memory, concentration problems, numbness, tingling, nerve pain, muscle weakness, hair loss and so on — I mean, these are similar to MS symptoms," Elliott said.

But she cautioned against concluding that Applegate's implants are responsible. "I'm not saying that Christina Applegate's breast implants are responsible for her symptoms," she said, adding that it would be "premature and irresponsible" to assume they explain them.
"Similar symptoms do not necessarily mean the same diagnosis," Elliott said. "Nothing should be overlooked or ruled out without being properly medically investigated."
Christina Applegate, left, arrives for the 29th Screen Actors Guild Awards in Century City, California, on Feb. 26, 2023. (Valerie Macon/AFP/Getty Images)
Dr. Stephen Nicolaidis, a Montreal plastic surgeon who says he's seen more than 1,500 patients for implant removal, also emphasized the need to investigate other possible causes.

He described BII as a "diagnosis of exclusion," where patients "have to be evaluated thoroughly, and then if they don't find something else as the cause, you should consider the possibility that the implants might be contributing to the problems."

Nicolaidis said symptoms he commonly hears about include fatigue, hair loss, skin rashes, breathing difficulties, joint and muscle pain, sleep problems and brain fog. Some can overlap with symptoms associated with autoimmune conditions.

Referencing Applegate's publicly described symptoms, he said, "Those symptoms that she had can very much be attributable to her breast implants." But the cause of BII is not established, and he said researchers do not yet have definitive answers about how implants might contribute to symptoms.

There is no specific test that can diagnose BII, Nicolaidis said. Imaging may show silicone outside an implant, but he said that finding is not required for someone to report symptoms. He also stressed that BII is different from implant-associated lymphoma, a cancer linked to certain textured implants.
Rupture, removal and next steps

A rupture or leak is a separate concern from BII. The FDA lists rupture and deflation among possible implant complications and advises patients to discuss new or unusual breast changes with a health-care provider.

Similarly, Health Canada advises people with implants to check regularly for unusual breast changes and discuss signs or symptoms with their doctor. Decisions about keeping, replacing or removing implants should be made with a clinician after considering individual symptoms, possible causes and surgical risks, the agency said.
It does not recommend preventive implant removal because surgery carries risks, and advises people experiencing symptoms to discuss them with a health-care provider.

items: Struggling with pain for years, N.S. woman heads to Montreal for breast implant removal
The costly, complex and dangerous world of removing medical devices | The Implant Files

blocks.text: Nicolaidis advised people with symptoms to seek a thorough medical evaluation. He said if other causes are not found, they can discuss whether implants might be contributing and weigh options with their clinicians.

He stopped placing breast implants in 2021 because he came to believe their risks outweighed their benefits in many cases, and now focuses largely on implant removal. He adds that removal is not a guaranteed cure. Nicolaidis said some patients he has treated with MS reported only slight improvement, and people with a diagnosed autoimmune disease may still need medical treatment after removal, known as explant surgery.

Elliott said she believes implant-related symptoms should be taken seriously, while acknowledging that their causes are not fully understood. She urged patients to seek balanced, evidence-based information and keep track of changes in their health.
"The fact that we do not have all the answers does not mean women's experiences should be dismissed," she said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Christine Pagulayan is a Toronto-based producer and writer with CBC News, currently with the Entertainment unit. She has worked in various roles at CBC News Network and The National. She has also worked as a multiplatform reporter in Toronto, Winnipeg, Halifax and Moncton. You can reach her at christine.pagulayan@cbc.ca.

In a Thursday update, EducationPlannerBC says that, on Nov. 3, it identified a "cybersecurity incident affecting its application system."
EducationPlannerBC says it's working with post-secondary institutions to 'minimize impacts' on applicants
The application portal for public post-secondary institutions in British Columbia has been temporarily offline for over a week following a data breach.

It confirmed "an unauthorized actor gained access to a limited amount of applicant data including applicant names, contact details and gender," but said information such as social insurance numbers, banking or financial information were not accessed.

The update went on to say EducationPlannerBC "recognizes that being offline may cause concern for applicants with upcoming program deadlines and is working closely with its post-secondary institutional partners to minimize impacts on applicants."

blocks.text: In a statement, the University of British Columbia says it's committed to ensuring no student application is adversely affected by the outage.

articles.title: Pfizer ends sale of hormone therapy cream Premarin in Canada
articles.summary: Pfizer will no longer sell its hormone replacement therapy Premarin in Canada following an internal review. The product has been available as a vaginal cream and three strengths of oral tablets.

image.caption: Pfizer says they will no longer sell vaginal cream Premarin in Canada following an internal review. The cream is used to treat menopause symptoms. (Maxim Shemetov/Reuters)

blocks.text: Health·New
Pfizer will no longer sell its hormone replacement therapy Premarin in Canada following an internal review. The product has been available as a vaginal cream and three strengths of oral tablets.
Other hormone replacement products prescribed to treat menopause also facing supply constraints
Premarin vaginal cream, which is used to treat symptoms of menopause, is currently unavailable and will not be returning, CBC News has confirmed.

According to Pfizer Canada’s pharmaceutical customer service centre, the company will no longer be marketing Premarin vaginal cream and Premarin tablets, although the tablets are expected to remain available through mid-2027.
Pfizer Canada told Reuters that there's been a shortage of the vaginal cream in Canada since June.

Demand for hormone replacement therapy has been rising, particularly in the United States, where prescriptions have increased following the U.S. Food and Drug Association's November 2025 removal of long-standing safety warnings from the treatments.

Some other hormone therapy products to treat menopause symptoms are also facing supply constraints in Canada. Earlier this month, Health Canada said certain strengths of estradiol transdermal patches made by Bayer and Sandoz Canada were in short supply, with intermittent shortages expected to continue until early 2027.
The discontinuation of Premarin products, alongside shortages of some estradiol patches, could add to pressure on Canada's menopause drug supply.

items: Unmanaged menopause symptoms cost Canada's economy $3.5B, experts tell MPs
More women are taking testosterone to treat menopause symptoms. Does science support that?

blocks.text: The decision was not related to any new safety, efficacy or quality concerns, Pfizer told Reuters, adding that other treatment options were available in Canada.

Existing inventories of Premarin tablets in 0.3 milligram, 0.625 mg and 1.25 mg strengths are expected to last until about mid-2027, although stocks could run out sooner if demand increases, the company said.
Why are some women taking testosterone to manage menopause?

The move follows a separate supply disruption in India, where Pfizer suspended sales of Premarin vaginal cream in July, Reuters reported at the time. The company had said it was exploring options to resume supplies.
Pfizer said its latest decision applied only to Canada and declined to comment on supply situations in other markets, Reuters reported.
The treatment contains a mixture ​of estrogen hormones and is prescribed to treat vaginal dryness, painful intercourse and other symptoms of menopause caused by declining estrogen levels.
Premarin cream and tablets are sold around the world, including in the U.S., Canada, New Zealand, Australia and Singapore.
Premarin Intravenous, used in hospitals for the treatment of abnormal uterine bleeding due to hormonal imbalance, is not affected.

articles.title: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
articles.summary: US lawmakers now want to question Huang over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.

blocks.text: Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, sending shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill.
Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.
One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future.
His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks.
Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected those allegations as a smear.
And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on his alleged affair.
If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC.
Representatives of Nvidia have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.
The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.
Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.
Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.
"Obviously, his behaviour has compounded over time," one long-time tech industry executive said, noting that other executives had been embroiled in revelations of infidelity.
Bill Gates of Microsoft and Jeff Bezos of Amazon had affairs exposed in the last decade. Both men are now divorced from their wives.
Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.
Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.
Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.
Because of Nvidia's size and success in recent years, such a drop can have a direct impact on the savings accounts of ordinary Americans.
Nvidia's value makes up about 7% of the S&P 500 index. That index is offered as a popular index fund in US retirement savings accounts.
Those account balances rise and fall with the changes of the stock market.

articles.title: Supreme Court orders probe into Basilan judge's killing in Zamboanga
articles.summary: Wee Sit, who presided over a Regional Trial Court branch, was gunned down Thursday.

blocks.text: Headlines
November 13, 2026 | 7:00am
This file photo shows the seal of the Supreme Court.
Philstar.com / EC Toledo
MANILA, Philippines — Supreme Court has ordered its judicial marshals to help investigate the killing of a Basilan judge who was shot dead in Zamboanga City on Thursday morning, November 12.
Presiding Judge Joseph Wee Sit of the Regional Trial Court Branch 2 in Isabela City, Basilan, was gunned down along Tumaga-Putik Road in Barangay Tumaga, Zamboanga City.

In a statement, the Supreme Court said it had mobilized the Office of the Judiciary Marshals to work with law enforcement authorities to establish the circumstances of the shooting and identify those responsible.
"Further details cannot be disclosed at this time to avoid compromising the investigation and the safety of those involved," the high court said.
The Supreme Court also warned that violence against judges threatens their ability to decide cases independently.

"Judges carry the difficult responsibility of deciding cases fairly and independently, even when their decisions may anger or disappoint others... In doing so, they face pressure, threats, and even danger to their own lives," it said. "Yet judges must continue to do their work without fear or favor."
Assistance for slain judge's family

Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda also directed the Office of the Court Administrator, through the regional court manager and executive judge, to personally coordinate with Wee Sit's family and ensure the prompt delivery of financial and institutional assistance.
Born in Zamboanga City on Nov. 21, 1987, Wee Sit earned his law degree from Western Mindanao State University and was admitted to the Philippine Bar in 2015.
He served as a prosecutor and public attorney before joining the judiciary on Sept. 23, 2025, less than 14 months before his killing.

"The killing of Judge Wee Sit is a painful reminder of the dangers faced by those who serve in our courts. No judge should have to fear for their life simply for doing their duty," the Supreme Court said.
"When judges are threatened or attacked, it is not only their safety that is at stake, but also the ability of our courts to deliver justice freely and independently."
The high court also cited a question once posed by former Chief Justice Artemio Panganiban: "How can judges give justice to the people when they themselves are victims of injustice?"

"Anumang karahasan laban sa ating mga hukom ay matinding banta sa katarungan at ating kalayaan. Kapag ang mga hukom ay tinatakot, napipigilan silang maghatid ng patas na desisyon. Ito ay panganib sa sistema ng katarungan at sa mga mamamayang umaasa rito upang maprotektahan ang kanilang mga karapatan," the Supreme Court said.

("Any violence against our judges is a serious threat to justice and our freedom. When judges are intimidated, they are prevented from delivering fair decisions. This endangers the justice system and the people who rely on it to protect their rights.")
